title.zh: 卷四百〇九 列傳第一百六十八 高定子 高斯得 張忠恕 唐璘
title.en: Volume 409 Biographies 168: Gao Dingzi, Gao Side, Zhang Zhongshu, Tang Lin
title.raw: 卷四百〇九 列傳第一百六十八 高定子 高斯得 張忠恕 唐璘 Volume 409 Biographies 168: Gao Dingzi, Gao Side, Zhang Zhongshu, Tang Lin

sentences.zh: 高定子高斯得張忠恕唐璘

translations.literal: Gao Dingzi, Gao Side, Zhang Zhongshu, Tang Lin
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dingzi, Gao Side, Zhang Zhongshu, and Tang Lin

sentences.zh: 高定子，字瞻叔，利州路提點刑獄兼知沔州稼之弟也。

translations.literal: Gao Dingzi, courtesy name Zhanshu, was the younger brother of Jia, who had been judicial intendant of Lizhou Circuit and concurrently prefect of Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dingzi, styled Zhanshu, was the younger brother of Gao Jia, who had served as judicial intendant for Lizhou Circuit and concurrent prefect of Mian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰二年舉進士，授郪縣主簿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiatai he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Qi County.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1202 and was appointed chief clerk of Qi County.

sentences.zh: 吳曦畔，乞解官養母，曦誅，攝府事宇文公紹以忠孝兩全薦之，調中江縣丞。

translations.literal: When Wu Xi rebelled, he requested to resign his office to care for his mother; after Xi was executed, Yuwen Gongshao, who was acting in prefectural affairs, recommended him as fulfilling both loyalty and filial piety, and he was transferred to assistant magistrate of Zhongjiang County.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi rebelled, he asked leave of his post to nurse his mother. After Xi's execution, Yuwen Gongshao, then acting prefect, commended his conduct as combining loyalty and filial duty and had him transferred to assistant magistrate of Zhongjiang.

sentences.zh: 父就養得疾，定子衣不解帶者六旬。

translations.literal: When his father came to live with him and fell ill, Dingzi went sixty days without undoing his belt.
translations.idiomatic: When his father came to live with him and fell ill, Dingzi attended him at bedside for sixty days without undressing for sleep.

sentences.zh: 居喪，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: In mourning he was so grief-stricken that he became emaciated to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he was so grief-stricken that he wasted away to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 服除，成都府路諸司辟丹棱令，尋以同產弟魏了翁守眉，改監資州酒務。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, the various offices of Chengdu Fu Circuit recruited him as magistrate of Danling; soon because his uterine brother Wei Liaoweng was defending Meizhou, he was changed to superintendent of the Zizhou liquor monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning, offices of Chengdu Circuit appointed him magistrate of Danling. Soon, because his full brother Wei Liaoweng was serving as prefect of Meizhou, he was reassigned to oversee the Zizhou liquor monopoly.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，差知夾江縣。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; when mourning ended he was assigned as magistrate of Jiajiang County.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother, he was appointed magistrate of Jiajiang County.

sentences.zh: 前是，酒酤貸秫於商人，定子給錢以糴，且寬榷酤，民以為便。

translations.literal: Previously the liquor monopoly had lent grain to merchants; Dingzi paid cash to buy grain and also relaxed the monopoly levies, which the people found convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the liquor monopoly had advanced grain to merchants on credit; Dingzi paid cash to purchase grain and eased the monopoly restrictions, to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 麻菽舊有征，定子悉弛之。

translations.literal: Hemp and beans had formerly been taxed; Dingzi abolished all such levies.
translations.idiomatic: Hemp and legumes had long been taxed; Dingzi abolished every such levy.

sentences.zh: 會水潦洊饑，貧民競訴無所於糴，定子曰：“汝毋憂，汝第持錢往常所糴家以俟。

translations.literal: When floods brought repeated famine, the poor clamored that they had nowhere to buy grain; Dingzi said, "Do not worry—just take your money to the houses where you usually buy grain and wait."
translations.idiomatic: When flooding brought repeated famine, the poor protested that they had nowhere to buy grain. Dingzi told them, "Do not worry—take your money to the shops where you usually buy and wait."

sentences.zh: ”乃發縣廩給諸富家，俾以時價糶，至秋而償，須臾米溢於市。

translations.literal: " He then released the county granary to supply wealthy households, enabling them to sell at market price and repay in autumn; in no time rice overflowed the market.
translations.idiomatic: " He then drew on the county granary to supply wealthy households, letting them sell at fair prices and repay in autumn; within moments the market was flooded with rice.

sentences.zh: 鄰邑有爭田十餘年不決，部使者以屬定子，定子察知偽為質劑，其人不伏。

translations.literal: A neighboring county had a land dispute unresolved for more than ten years; the circuit envoy assigned it to Dingzi, who detected that the deed of proof was forged, but the man would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: A neighboring county had a land dispute that had gone unresolved for over ten years. The circuit envoy referred it to Dingzi, who found the title deed forged, but the claimant refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 定子曰：“嘉定改元詔三月始至縣，安得有嘉定元年正月文書邪？

translations.literal: Dingzi said, "The decree changing the era name to Jiading did not reach the county until the third month—how could there be a document dated the first month of the first year of Jiading?"
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi said, "The Jiading era-change edict did not reach this county until the third month—how could there be a document dated the first month of Jiading year one?"

sentences.zh: ”兩造遂決。

translations.literal: " The two parties were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: " The case was then closed.

sentences.zh: 四川總領所辟主管文字，同幕有以趣辦為能迫促諸郡者，定子白使者斥去之。

translations.literal: The Sichuan General Superintendency recruited him as chief clerk for documents; a colleague in the secretariat who prided himself on rapid fulfillment and pressed the various prefectures—Dingzi reported to the commissioner and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan General Superintendency recruited him as chief clerk for documents. When a colleague who prided himself on rapid fulfillment and hectored the prefectures, Dingzi reported to the commissioner and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 總領所治利州，倚酒榷以佐軍用，吏奸盤錯，定子躬自究詰，酒政遂平。

translations.literal: The superintendency governed Lizhou and relied on the liquor monopoly to support military expenses; official corruption was tangled and deep; Dingzi personally investigated, and the liquor administration was set right.
translations.idiomatic: The superintendency was based at Lizhou and relied on the liquor monopoly to fund the army. Corruption among the clerks was rampant; Dingzi investigated personally, and the liquor administration was brought into order.

sentences.zh: 後來者復欲增課，定子曰：“前以吏蠹，亦既革之，今又求益，是再榷也。

translations.literal: His successor again wished to increase the levy; Dingzi said, "Previously because of official corruption it was reformed; now you seek more—this is to monopolize a second time."
translations.idiomatic: His successor again sought to raise the levy. Dingzi said, "We reformed the system because of official corruption; to demand more now is to impose a second monopoly."

sentences.zh: ”乃止。

translations.literal: " It was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The increase was dropped.

sentences.zh: 製置使鄭損強愎自用，誤謂總領所擅十一州小會子之利，奏請廢之，令下，民疑而罷市。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner Zheng Sun was obstinate and self-willed; he mistakenly believed the superintendency had usurped the profits of the small huizi notes of eleven prefectures and memorialized to abolish them; when the order was issued, the people were suspicious and markets ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Zheng Sun was stubborn and self-willed. Mistakenly believing the superintendency had monopolized profits from the small huizi notes of eleven prefectures, he memorialized to abolish them. When the order came down, the people grew uneasy and markets shut down.

sentences.zh: 定子力爭，謂：“小會子實以代錢，百姓貿易，賴是以權川引，罷則關、隴之民交病，況又隆興間得旨為之，非擅也。

translations.literal: Dingzi argued forcefully, saying, "The small huizi in fact substitute for coin; the people trade relying on them to balance Sichuan's currency; if abolished, the people of the passes and Long region will all suffer; moreover, during Longxing an imperial edict authorized them—it was not usurpation."
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi argued vigorously: "The small huizi truly serve as money substitutes. The people rely on them in trade to balance Sichuan's currency. Abolishing them would afflict everyone in the frontier passes and Long region. Moreover, an imperial edict during Longxing authorized their use—this was no usurpation."

sentences.zh: ”乃得存其半。

translations.literal: " They were then allowed to retain half.
translations.idiomatic: " Half the issue was preserved.

sentences.zh: 損又欲增總領所鹽課，取舊貸軍費，定子辨其顛末，損乃釋然曰：“二司相關處，公每明白洞達言之，使人爽然自失。

translations.literal: Sun again wished to increase the superintendency's salt levy and take back old military loans; Dingzi explained the full sequence of events; Sun then said with relief, "Where the two offices intersect, you always speak with such clear penetration that one feels suddenly abashed."
translations.idiomatic: Sun again sought to raise the superintendency's salt levy and reclaim old military loans. Dingzi explained the full history of the matter. Sun then said with relief, "Whenever our two offices overlap, you explain things so clearly that one is left abashed."

sentences.zh: ”尋差知長寧軍。

translations.literal: " Soon he was assigned as magistrate of Changning Army.
translations.idiomatic: " He was soon appointed magistrate of Changning Army.

sentences.zh: 長寧地接夷獠，公家百需皆仰淯井鹽利，來者往往因以自封殖，製置司又榷入其半。

translations.literal: Changning bordered Yi and Liao peoples; all public needs relied on Yujing salt profits; incoming officials often used this to enrich themselves, and the pacification office again monopolized half.
translations.idiomatic: Changning bordered tribal territories; all public needs depended on Yujing salt revenues. Incoming officials often used this to enrich themselves, and the pacification office again seized half through monopoly.

sentences.zh: 定子至，爭於製置使，得蠲重賦。

translations.literal: When Dingzi arrived, he disputed with the pacification commissioner and obtained remission of heavy levies.
translations.idiomatic: On arriving, Dingzi pressed the pacification commissioner and secured remission of heavy levies.

sentences.zh: 差知綿州。

translations.literal: He was assigned as magistrate of Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 大元兵穿鳳州塞，破武休，下興元，小校張鉞以其徒潰入文州，殺守臣楊必復，將自龍趨綿，以闖成都。

translations.literal: Great Yuan troops broke through Fengzhou pass, defeated Wuxiu, descended on Xingyuan; the petty officer Zhang Yue led his men in rout into Wenzhou, killed the defending official Yang Bifu, and intended to advance from Long toward Mian to burst into Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan forces broke through Fengzhou pass, took Wuxiu, and descended on Xingyuan. A junior officer, Zhang Yue, led his routed men into Wenzhou, killed the defending official Yang Bifu, and planned to march from Longzhou toward Mianzhou to strike at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 安撫使黃伯固聞之，亟奏定子兼參議官，措置文、龍備禦。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Huang Bogu heard of it and urgently memorialized to make Dingzi concurrently a deliberation officer to arrange defenses for Wen and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Huang Bogu heard of this and urgently memorialized to appoint Dingzi concurrently as deliberation officer to organize the defenses of Wen and Long prefectures.

sentences.zh: 定子乃部分諸軍扼青塘嶺，鉞就擒。

translations.literal: Dingzi then deployed the various armies to hold Qingtang Ridge, and Yue was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi deployed the armies to hold Qingtang Ridge, and Yue was captured.

sentences.zh: 已而劍南大震，定子語僚吏曰：“諸君去留不敢拘，若某則守城郭封疆之臣，有死而已。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Jiannan was greatly shaken; Dingzi told his staff, "You gentlemen may stay or go as you wish—I dare not constrain you; as for me, I am a minister who guards walls and frontiers, and have only death."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiannan was thrown into turmoil. Dingzi told his staff, "You may stay or go as you wish—I will not constrain you. As for me, I am a frontier official charged with guarding walls and borders, and I have only death."

sentences.zh: ”戒群胥曰：“潰軍流民不過欲得錢糧爾，吾將盡發吾州之藏與截諸司之綱，為朝廷捍蔽全蜀。

translations.literal: " He warned all clerks, "Routed troops and displaced people only want money and grain; I shall exhaust this prefecture's stores and intercept the various offices' transport funds to shield all of Shu for the court."
translations.idiomatic: " He warned his clerks, "Routed soldiers and refugees only want pay and grain. I will empty this prefecture's stores and divert funds from other agencies to shield all of Shu for the throne."

sentences.zh: 我去，聽汝等殺我；

translations.literal: If I go, you may kill me;
translations.idiomatic: If I leave, you may kill me;

sentences.zh: 汝等逃，吾斫汝頭矣。

translations.literal: if you flee, I shall cut off your heads."
translations.idiomatic: if you flee, I will cut off your heads."

sentences.zh: ”乃下令招潰卒，人給緡錢五十、米一石，命都監陳訓專任接納。

translations.literal: " He then ordered to recruit routed soldiers, giving each fifty strings of cash and one shi of rice, and commanded Metropolitan Supervisor Chen Xun to take sole charge of receiving them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered to recruit routed troops, paying each fifty strings of cash and one shi of rice, and put Metropolitan Supervisor Chen Xun in charge of receiving them.

sentences.zh: 訓忽奔告曰：“諸軍雖受招，不肯釋甲，奈何？

translations.literal: Xun suddenly ran in reporting, "The armies though recruited will not lay down their armor—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Xun suddenly rushed in to report, "The troops have accepted recruitment but refuse to lay down their arms—what can we do?"

sentences.zh: ”定子乃令帳下卒衷甲於兩廡以俟，戒毋輕動。

translations.literal: " Dingzi then ordered his personal troops to don armor hidden in both side halls and wait, warning them not to move lightly.
translations.idiomatic: " Dingzi had his personal guards don armor in the side halls and wait, warning them not to act rashly.

sentences.zh: 俄而諸軍盛陳兵以至，吏士皆股栗，定子坐堂上，傳令勞苦之，諸軍皆拜。

translations.literal: Soon the armies arrived in full array of arms; clerks and officers all trembled in their legs; Dingzi sat in the hall and sent orders to comfort them with toil; all the armies bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the troops arrived in full battle array. Clerks and officers trembled with fear. Dingzi sat in the hall and sent word to commend their hardships; the soldiers all bowed.

sentences.zh: 定子開諭以理，使還本部，以俟給犒。

translations.literal: Dingzi enlightened them with reason and had them return to their original units to await distribution of rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi reasoned with them and sent them back to their units to await their rewards.

sentences.zh: 諸將聞之，亦來上謁，定子復慰安之。

translations.literal: The various generals hearing of it also came to pay respects; Dingzi again comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, other generals also came to pay their respects, and Dingzi reassured them as well.

sentences.zh: 因問：“汝等何為至此？

translations.literal: He then asked, "Why have you come here?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked, "Why have you come here?"

sentences.zh: ”皆曰：“製置使未知存亡，諸軍無主。

translations.literal: " All said, "The pacification commissioner is not known whether alive or dead; the armies have no leader."
translations.idiomatic: " They all said, "We do not know whether the pacification commissioner is alive or dead, and the armies have no commander."

sentences.zh: ”定子曰：“大帥不過暫移治爾，已遣人訪所在，苟終不獲，我當為汝曹主張。

translations.literal: " Dingzi said, "The great commander has only temporarily moved his administration; I have already sent men to seek his whereabouts; if he is ultimately not found, I shall act on your behalf."
translations.idiomatic: " Dingzi said, "The commander has only temporarily relocated. I have already sent men to find him. If he cannot be found, I will act on your behalf."

sentences.zh: 且諸軍至此以無糧故，吾州當任供億。

translations.literal: Moreover, the armies have come here because of lack of grain; this prefecture must bear the responsibility of supply."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, you have come because you lack grain. This prefecture will take responsibility for supplying you."

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“敵將復會於此，盍避之？

translations.literal: " He also said, "The enemy will again assemble here—why not avoid it?"
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "The enemy will gather here again—why not withdraw?"

sentences.zh: ”定子曰：“我文官也，不畏死，汝將軍也，世世衣食縣官，乃欲避敵乎？

translations.literal: " Dingzi said, "I am a civil official and do not fear death; you are generals who generation after generation eat and clothe yourselves from the state's pay—yet you wish to avoid the enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: " Dingzi said, "I am a civil official and do not fear death. You are generals who have lived for generations on the state's pay—yet you wish to flee the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 我是守臣，死則死於此爾。

translations.literal: I am the defending minister; if I die, I die here.
translations.idiomatic: I am the defending official; if I die, I die here.

sentences.zh: 有欲殺太守者，一槍足矣，軍器安用多為？

translations.literal: If anyone wishes to kill the prefect, one spear is enough—why need so many weapons?
translations.idiomatic: If anyone wishes to kill the prefect, one spear is enough—why carry so many weapons?

sentences.zh: 今諸軍大集，萬一敵至，能戮力出戰，是汝曹立功報國之機也，不猶愈於深入內郡為罪滋大乎？

translations.literal: Now that the armies are gathered in force, if by chance the enemy comes and you can unite in battle, this is your chance to achieve merit and repay the state—is it not better than penetrating deep into inner prefectures where your guilt would be greater?
translations.idiomatic: Now that you are gathered here, if the enemy comes and you fight together, this is your chance to win merit and serve the state—is that not better than pushing deep into inner prefectures where your crimes would be far worse?

sentences.zh: ”眾悅而去。

translations.literal: " The crowd was pleased and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " The men were satisfied and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 乃遣吏給犒如令，辟寺觀祠宇以舍之。

translations.literal: He then sent clerks to distribute rewards as ordered and requisitioned temples and shrines to lodge them.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent clerks to distribute rewards as promised and requisitioned temples and shrines to house the troops.

sentences.zh: 亡幾何，敗將和彥威、陳邦佐、曹篪、張涓、姚承祖等皆集於彰明，剽掠尤甚。

translations.literal: Before long, defeated generals He Yanwei, Chen Bangzuo, Cao Chi, Zhang Juan, Yao Chengzu, and others all gathered at Zhangming, plundering especially severely.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, defeated generals He Yanwei, Chen Bangzuo, Cao Chi, Zhang Juan, Yao Chengzu, and others gathered at Zhangming, plundering with particular violence.

sentences.zh: 彥威遣邦佐入州，大言駭眾，謂定子曰：“知府何不去？

translations.literal: Yanwei sent Bangzuo into the prefecture with grand words to terrify the crowd, saying to Dingzi, "Why does the prefect not leave?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei sent Bangzuo into the prefecture with bluster to intimidate the people, telling Dingzi, "Why does the prefect not leave?"

sentences.zh: 和太尉兼兩戎司，威權甚重，麾下兵且二萬餘，欲來駐此，今至矣。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal He concurrently holds both military commissions; his authority is very weighty; the troops under him number more than twenty thousand; he wishes to station here—he has now arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal He holds both military commissions; his authority is immense, and he commands more than twenty thousand men. He intends to encamp here—and he has now arrived.

sentences.zh: ”定子謂曰：“本州素非備禦之地，大將以兵入，欲何為者？

translations.literal: " Dingzi said to him, "This prefecture has never been a place of defense; the great general brings troops in—what does he intend?"
translations.idiomatic: " Dingzi replied, "This prefecture has never been a defensive post. What does the general intend by marching troops in?"

sentences.zh: 第來，吾固有以相待。

translations.literal: Just come—I naturally have means to receive you."
translations.idiomatic: Let him come—I have my own way of receiving him."

sentences.zh: ”邦佐色沮，乃曰：“已遣幕府來議。

translations.literal: " Bangzuo's color fell, and he then said, "I have already sent the staff to negotiate."
translations.idiomatic: " Bangzuo's face fell, and he said, "I have already sent staff to negotiate."

sentences.zh: ”至則一遊士爾，繆為恭敬，要索甚大。

translations.literal: " When he arrived it was only a wandering scholar, falsely showing respect, demanding very much.
translations.idiomatic: " When he arrived, it was only a wandering scholar who feigned respect while making enormous demands.

sentences.zh: 定子答曰：“軍將入吾境，當受吾節製，惟各守紀律，則給以錢糧。

translations.literal: Dingzi answered, "When troops enter my territory they must accept my control; only if each keeps discipline will I supply money and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi answered, "Troops entering my jurisdiction must accept my authority. Only if you keep discipline will I supply pay and grain."

sentences.zh: 若敵至，為國一死，作忠臣孝子，愈於病五日不汗死也。

translations.literal: If the enemy comes, to die once for the state and become a loyal minister and filial son is better than dying of illness after five days without sweating.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy comes, to die for the state as a loyal minister and filial son is better than wasting away for five days without breaking a sweat.

sentences.zh: ”幕府莫能對，出彥威符移，有云：“大府招戢散軍，人給錢米若干，今所部不下二萬人，願如數得之。

translations.literal: " The staff could not reply; they produced Yanwei's official dispatch, which said, "The great prefecture recruits and pacifies scattered troops, giving each a certain amount of money and rice; my command now numbers no fewer than twenty thousand—I wish to receive the full amount."
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy had no reply. He produced Yanwei's official dispatch: "The great prefecture recruits scattered troops and pays each a set amount of money and rice. My command now numbers at least twenty thousand—I expect payment in full."

sentences.zh: ”定子報曰：“本州已下此令，何敢食言；

translations.literal: " Dingzi replied, "This prefecture has already issued this order—how dare I break my word;"
translations.idiomatic: " Dingzi replied, "This prefecture has already issued that order—I would not break my word;"

sentences.zh: 但所給者乃潰軍就招免罪之人，都統所部非潰也，若以此例相給，其肯受乎？

translations.literal: but what is given is to routed troops who accept recruitment to escape punishment; the metropolitan commander's troops are not routed—if you are supplied by this precedent, would they accept it?"
translations.idiomatic: but that payment is for routed troops who accept recruitment to escape punishment. The metropolitan commander's men are not routed troops. If you were paid on the same terms, would they accept it?"

sentences.zh: ”彥威得檄甚慚，乃乞別給錢糧以餉軍，定子即捐四十萬緡與之，仍趣其還戍。

translations.literal: " Yanwei receiving the dispatch was deeply ashamed and then begged separate payment of money and grain to supply the army; Dingzi immediately contributed four hundred thousand strings to him and still urged him to return to garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanwei was deeply shamed by the reply and begged separate funds to supply his army. Dingzi immediately contributed four hundred thousand strings of cash and urged him to return to his post.

sentences.zh: 蓋定子身任兩司之責，極其勞勩，以收捕張鉞功，進三官，以防遏招收潰兵功，又進一官，進直寶章閣，再任。

translations.literal: In sum Dingzi personally bore the responsibilities of two offices, exhausting his labor; for the merit of capturing Zhang Yue he was advanced three ranks; for the merit of preventing and recruiting routed troops he was advanced one more rank, promoted to Direct Attendant of the Baozhang Pavilion, and served a second term.
translations.idiomatic: In all, Dingzi personally shouldered the duties of two offices and exhausted himself in the effort. For capturing Zhang Yue he was promoted three ranks; for containing and recruiting routed troops he gained another promotion, was made Direct Attendant of the Baozhang Pavilion, and served a second term.

sentences.zh: 頃之，召入奏事，吏民追送，莫不流涕；

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to report on affairs; clerks and people pursued to send him off, none without shedding tears;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned to court. Clerks and commoners ran after him in farewell, all in tears;

sentences.zh: 鄰郡聞定子至，焚香夾道，舉手加額曰：“微公，吾屬塗炭久矣。

translations.literal: neighboring prefectures hearing Dingzi had come burned incense lining the roads, raised hands to their foreheads and said, "But for you, sir, we would long have been in misery."
translations.idiomatic: neighboring prefectures, hearing Dingzi was passing through, burned incense along the roads and cried with hands raised, "But for you, sir, we would long have been in misery."

sentences.zh: ”定子之未去郡也，伯兄稼以權利路提刑上印而歸，了翁亦至自靖州，過定子於綿，定子為築棣鄂堂，飲酒賦詩為樂，一時以為美談。

translations.literal: " Before Dingzi left the prefecture, his elder brother Jia had returned after surrendering the seal as acting judicial intendant of Lizhou; Liaoweng also arrived from Jingzhou; passing Dingzi at Mian, Dingzi built the Di'e Hall for him; they drank wine and composed poetry for pleasure—a story admired at the time.
translations.idiomatic: " Before leaving the prefecture, his elder brother Gao Jia had returned after relinquishing his acting post as Lizhou judicial intendant, and Wei Liaoweng arrived from Jingzhou. Meeting Dingzi at Mianzhou, Dingzi built the Di'e Hall for them; they drank and composed poetry for pleasure—a story much admired at the time.

sentences.zh: 入對，極言時敝。

translations.literal: Entering audience, he spoke to the utmost of the times' abuses.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he spoke at length on the abuses of the age.

sentences.zh: 時史彌遠執國柄久，故有曰：“陛下優禮元勳，俾得以弛繁機而養靜壽，朝廷得以新百度而革因循，不亦善乎？

translations.literal: At the time Shi Miyuan had long held state power, so he had said, "Your Majesty treats the founding meritocrats with favor, enabling them to relax heavy duties and nurture quiet longevity; the court can renew all measures and reform routine—is this not good?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan had long held state power, so he said, "Your Majesty honors the founding meritocrats, allowing them to lay aside heavy duties and live in quiet retirement, while the court renews all measures and breaks free of routine—is that not wise?"

sentences.zh: ”既對，人為定子危之，定子曰：“乖逢得喪，是有命焉，吾得盡言，乃報君職分也。

translations.literal: " After the audience people worried for Dingzi; Dingzi said, "Fortune and misfortune, gain and loss—all have fate; that I could speak fully is repaying my duty to the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: " After the audience people feared for his safety. Dingzi said, "Fortune and misfortune are ordained by fate. To speak my mind fully is simply to fulfill my duty to the sovereign."

sentences.zh: ”越兩月，乃遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: " After two months he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: " Two months later he was appointed Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 彌遠沒，言之者紛然，識者謂定子先事有言，視諸人為難。

translations.literal: When Miyuan died, those who spoke were numerous; the knowing said Dingzi had spoken beforehand on the matter, regarding others as difficult.
translations.idiomatic: When Miyuan died, many spoke out. Observers noted that Dingzi had spoken out beforehand, which made him stand apart from the rest.

sentences.zh: 尋以直寶謨閣、江南東路轉運判官。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Direct Attendant of the Baomo Pavilion and Transport Vice Commissioner of Jiangnan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Direct Attendant of the Baomo Pavilion and Transport Vice Commissioner for Jiangnan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，帝曰：“淮師巡邊，卿知之乎？

translations.literal: At farewell audience the emperor said, "The Huai armies are patrolling the border—do you know of it?"
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor said, "The Huai armies are patrolling the frontier—are you aware of this?"

sentences.zh: 輔車之勢，漕運為急，卿是行宜斟酌緩急，以相通融。

translations.literal: Like cheek and cart, transport is urgent; on this mission you should weigh urgency and ease to achieve mutual accommodation."
translations.idiomatic: Like the cheek and the jawbone, transport is critical. On this mission you should weigh priorities and coordinate them flexibly."

sentences.zh: ” 定子因上疏論邊事甚周悉，帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: Dingzi then submitted a memorial discussing border affairs very comprehensively; the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi submitted a memorial on border affairs that was thorough and comprehensive, and the emperor commended and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 逾年，召入奏事。

translations.literal: After a year he was summoned to report on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 會稼死事於沔州，上疏引疾，乞歸田裏，不許。

translations.literal: It happened that Jia died in service at Mianzhou; he submitted a memorial citing illness and begged to return to his fields; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia died in service at Mianzhou, he memorialized citing illness and begged to retire to his home; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 尋遷軍器監，又遷太府少卿，升計度轉運副使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Armory Directorate, then to Vice Minister of the Treasury, and promoted to Vice Commissioner of Fiscal Planning and Transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Director of the Armory Directorate, then Vice Minister of the Treasury, and promoted to Vice Commissioner of Fiscal Planning and Transport.

sentences.zh: 有事於明堂，天大雷雨，詔求言，定子反覆論敬懼災異之意。

translations.literal: When there were rites at the Bright Hall, heaven sent great thunder and rain; an edict sought opinions; Dingzi repeatedly discussed the meaning of reverence and fear of portents.
translations.idiomatic: During rites at the Bright Hall, a great thunderstorm struck. The court called for memorials, and Dingzi repeatedly urged reverence and fear of heaven's warnings.

sentences.zh: 復召入，遷司農卿兼玉牒所檢討官。

translations.literal: He was again summoned in and transferred to Minister of Agriculture, concurrently Reviewing Official of the Jade Genealogy Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned again and made Minister of Agriculture, concurrently Reviewing Official of the Jade Genealogy Office.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：“內治不修，外懼不謹，近親有預政之漸，近習有弄權之漸，小人有復用之漸，國柄有陵夷之漸，士氣有委靡之漸，主勢有孤立之漸，宗社有阽危之漸。

translations.literal: Entering audience he said, "Internal governance is not cultivated, external fears are not heeded; close kin show signs of participating in government, close attendants show signs of manipulating power, petty men show signs of being reused, state authority shows signs of decline, scholarly morale shows signs of lassitude, sovereign power shows signs of isolation, altars of state show signs of peril."
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said, "Internal governance is neglected and external threats are ignored. Close kin are edging toward participation in government; close attendants toward manipulating power; petty men toward being restored to office; state authority toward decline; scholarly morale toward lassitude; the sovereign toward isolation; and the altars of state toward peril."

sentences.zh: 天變日多，地形日蹙。

translations.literal: Heavenly changes grow daily; territory shrinks daily.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly portents multiply daily, and the realm's territory shrinks daily.

sentences.zh: 昔有危脈，今有危形；

translations.literal: Formerly there was a perilous pulse; now there is a perilous form;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly there was a perilous pulse; now there is a perilous outward form;

sentences.zh: 昔有亡理，今有亡證。

translations.literal: formerly there was a principle of ruin; now there are proofs of ruin."
translations.idiomatic: formerly there was a logic of collapse; now there are signs of collapse."

sentences.zh: ”又請明詔沿流帥守將吏，思出奇乘險，求為水陸可進之策。

translations.literal: " He also requested a clear edict to commanders and officials along the rivers to think of striking by surprise over difficult terrain and seek strategies for advance by water and land.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked for a clear edict instructing commanders and officials along the rivers to devise bold stratagems exploiting difficult terrain and to seek viable routes of advance by land and water.

sentences.zh: 升兼樞密都承旨，又遷太常少卿兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to concurrently Chief Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently Compiler of the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to concurrently Chief Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then made Vice Minister of Rites and Compiler of the National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 累言邊事，遷起居舍人，尋兼中書舍人，參讚京湖、江西督視府事，定子親往周視新城，大犒諸軍，激厲守將。

translations.literal: Repeatedly speaking on border affairs, he was transferred to Attendant of the Imperial Diary, soon concurrently Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, assisting in the Jing-Hu and Jiangxi Supervisory Offices; Dingzi personally went to inspect Xincheng, greatly rewarded the armies, and exhorted the defending generals.
translations.idiomatic: After repeatedly memorializing on border affairs, he was made Attendant of the Imperial Diary and soon concurrently Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, assisting the Jing-Hu and Jiangxi supervisory offices. Dingzi personally inspected Xincheng, lavished rewards on the troops, and exhorted the defending generals.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎，仍兼中書舍人，即軍中賜金帶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, still concurrently Drafting Attendant, and in the army was bestowed a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites while retaining his post as Drafting Attendant, and was awarded a gold belt in the field.

sentences.zh: 詔以督府事入奏，既至，帝勞問甚渥，特進一官，尋兼崇政殿說書兼直學士院。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to report on supervisory office affairs; when he arrived the emperor comforted him very warmly, specially advanced him one rank, and soon made him concurrently Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall and Attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to report on supervisory affairs at court. On arrival the emperor received him with great warmth, granted him a special promotion, and soon made him Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall and Attendant of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改侍講、權禮部尚書，升兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Court Lecturer and Acting Minister of Rites, promoted to concurrently Court Reader.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Court Lecturer and Acting Minister of Rites, then promoted to concurrently Court Reader.

sentences.zh: 入奏，言：“國無仁賢，無禮義，無政事，有類叔世。

translations.literal: Entering to report he said, "The state lacks benevolent worthies, lacks ritual and righteousness, lacks governance—it resembles a declining age."
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said, "The state lacks benevolent worthies, ritual and righteousness, and sound governance—it resembles a declining age."

sentences.zh: ”帝竦然。

translations.literal: " The emperor was startled.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was startled.

sentences.zh: 尋兼直學士，修孝宗、寧宗《日曆》，書成上進，擢拜翰林學士、知制誥兼吏部尚書，升兼修國史、實錄院修撰，賜衣帶、鞍馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Direct Academician, compiled the Daily Records of Xiaozong and Ningzong; when the book was completed and submitted he was elevated and appointed Hanlin Academician, Drafter of Edicts, concurrently Minister of Personnel, promoted to concurrently Compiler of National History and Veritable Records, and granted robes, belt, and saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Direct Academician and compiled the Daily Records of Xiaozong and Ningzong. When the work was completed and submitted, he was elevated to Hanlin Academician, Drafter of Edicts, and concurrently Minister of Personnel, then promoted to Compiler of National History and Veritable Records, and granted robes, belt, and saddle horse.

sentences.zh: 乞召收李心傳卒成四朝誌、傳。

translations.literal: He requested to summon Li Xinchuan back to complete the chronicles and biographies of four reigns.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Li Xinchuan be recalled to finish the chronicles and biographies of four reigns.

sentences.zh: 時禮部尚書杜範、吏部侍郎李韶皆以伉直稱，或乞身求去，或臥家不出。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Rites Du Fan and Vice Minister of Personnel Li Shao were both known for upright bluntness; one begged leave to depart, the other lay at home and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Minister of Rites Du Fan and Vice Minister of Personnel Li Shao were both known for blunt integrity; one had begged to resign, the other had withdrawn to his home.

sentences.zh: 定子言：“人主寄耳目者，台諫也，補耳目之所不逮者，法從之論思，百官之輪對，則上必論君德之粹駁，次必言朝政之得失。

translations.literal: Dingzi said, "What the ruler entrusts as eyes and ears are the remonstrance bureaus; what supplements what eyes and ears cannot reach are the statutory attendants' deliberations and the hundred officials' rotating audiences—then above all one must discuss the purity or admixture of the ruler's virtue, next must speak of the gains and losses of court governance."
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi said, "The remonstrance bureaus are the ruler's eyes and ears. Statutory attendants' deliberations and the hundred officials' rotating audiences supplement what those eyes and ears cannot reach—first by assessing the ruler's virtue, then by discussing the gains and losses of court policy."

sentences.zh: 舍是而使之但言常程，姑應故事，畏縮乎雷霆之威，阿徇乎宰執之好，遜避乎耳目之官，則凡論思等事，皆不必講矣。

translations.literal: Apart from this, if one makes them speak only routine matters, merely respond to precedent, shrink before the thunder of authority, curry favor with the chief ministers' preferences, and yield before the eyes-and-ears officials—then all deliberation and the like need not be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: If instead they are made to speak only of routine business, merely go through the motions, shrink before imperial wrath, curry favor with the chief ministers, and defer to the remonstrance officials, then deliberation and candid counsel become pointless.

sentences.zh: 宜速返李韶以開不諱之門，勉起杜範以伸敢言之氣。

translations.literal: It is fitting quickly to recall Li Shao to open the gate of no taboo, and urge Du Fan to rise to extend the spirit of daring speech.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shao should be recalled at once to open the door to frank speech, and Du Fan should be urged to return to revive the spirit of bold remonstrance.

sentences.zh: ”因乞歸田甚力。

translations.literal: " He then begged very forcefully to return to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: " He then pressed his request to retire to his home fields with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 進端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事，尋兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Academician of the Duanming Hall and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, soon concurrently Acting Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician of the Duanming Hall and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and soon made Acting Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 仍舊職，知福州、福建安撫，固辭，提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Retaining his old posts, he was made prefect of Fuzhou and Fujian Pacification Commissioner; he firmly declined and was made Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: While retaining his existing posts, he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou and Fujian Pacification Commissioner. He firmly declined and was made Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace instead.

sentences.zh: 因請致仕，不許，改知潭州、湖南安撫大使，力辭，退居吳中，深衣大帶，日以著述自娛。

translations.literal: He then requested retirement; it was not granted; he was changed to prefect of Tanzhou and Great Pacification Commissioner of Hunan; he forcefully declined, retired to live in Wu, wore deep robes with broad sash, and daily amused himself with writing.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement but was refused, then was offered prefect of Tanzhou and Great Pacification Commissioner of Hunan. He declined forcefully, withdrew to Wu, dressed in plain scholar's robes, and devoted his days to writing.

sentences.zh: 以資政殿學士轉一官致仕，卒，贈少保。

translations.literal: As Academician of the Zizheng Hall he was advanced one rank and retired; he died and was posthumously granted Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: As Academician of the Zizheng Hall he received one final promotion and retired; he died and was posthumously granted the title Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 字子作同人書院於夾江，修長興學，創六先生祠，蓋以教化為先務。

translations.literal: He built the Tongren Academy at Jiajiang, restored the Changxing school, and founded a shrine to the Six Masters—education was his foremost task.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Tongren Academy at Jiajiang, restored the Changxing school, and established a shrine to the Six Masters, making education his foremost concern.

sentences.zh: 所著《存著齋文集》、《北門類稿》、《薇垣類稿》、《經說》、《紹熙講義》、《奏議》、《曆官表奏》行世。

translations.literal: His works in circulation include Collected Writings from the Cunzhu Studio, North Gate Miscellany, Wei Garden Miscellany, Expositions on the Classics, Shaoxi Lectures, Memorials, and Memorials from Official Posts.
translations.idiomatic: His works that circulated include the Collected Writings from the Cunzhu Studio, North Gate Miscellany, Wei Garden Miscellany, Expositions on the Classics, Shaoxi Lectures, Memorials, and Memorials from Official Posts.

sentences.zh: 高斯得字不妄，利州路提點刑獄、知沔州稼之子也。

translations.literal: Gao Side, courtesy name Buwang, was the son of Jia, judicial intendant of Lizhou Circuit and prefect of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Side, styled Buwang, was the son of Gao Jia, who had served as judicial intendant for Lizhou Circuit and prefect of Mian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少從李坤臣學，坤臣瞽，斯得左右扶持之。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Li Kunchen; Kunchen was blind, and Side supported him on either hand.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Li Kunchen, who was blind; Side attended and supported him on either side.

sentences.zh: 中成都路轉運司試，補入太學。

translations.literal: He passed the Chengdu Fu Circuit transport commission examination and was admitted to the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Chengdu Circuit transport commission examination and entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 紹定二年舉進士，授利州路觀察推官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoding he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed investigating and pushing official of Lizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1229 and was appointed investigating and pushing official for Lizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 越二年，辟差四川茶馬幹辦公事。

translations.literal: After two years he was recruited as acting handler of Sichuan tea-and-horse affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was recruited as acting handler of Sichuan tea-and-horse affairs.

sentences.zh: 李心傳以著作佐郎領史事，即成都修《國朝會要》，辟為檢閱文字。

translations.literal: Li Xinchuan as Assistant Compiler led historical work and at Chengdu compiled the National Dynastic Essentials; he recruited Side as reviewing clerk for texts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xinchuan, as Assistant Compiler, directed historical work and compiled the National Dynastic Essentials at Chengdu; he recruited Side as reviewing clerk.

sentences.zh: 端平二年九月，稼死事於沔，時大元兵屯沔，斯得日夜西向號泣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Duanping, Jia died in service at Mian; at the time Great Yuan troops were encamped at Mian; Side day and night faced west and wailed.
translations.idiomatic: In September 1235, Jia died in service at Mianzhou while Yuan troops were encamped there. Side faced west day and night, weeping and wailing.

sentences.zh: 會其僮至自沔，知稼戰沒處，與斯得潛行至其地，遂得稼遺體，奉以歸，見者感泣。

translations.literal: It happened that his servant boy arrived from Mian knowing where Jia fell in battle; with Side he secretly went to the place, thus obtained Jia's remains, and bore them home—those who saw it were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: When a servant arrived from Mian knowing where Jia had fallen, Side went secretly with him to the site, recovered his father's body, and brought it home. All who witnessed it were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 服除而哀傷不已，無意仕進。

translations.literal: When mourning ended his grief did not cease, and he had no mind for advancement in office.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended his grief did not abate, and he had no wish to pursue office.

sentences.zh: 心傳方修四朝史，辟為史館檢閱，秩同秘閣校勘，蓋創員也。

translations.literal: Xinchuan was compiling the history of four reigns and recruited him as History Institute reviewer, rank equal to Secretariat collator—a newly created post.
translations.idiomatic: While Xinchuan was compiling the history of four reigns, he recruited Side as History Institute reviewer with rank equal to Secretariat collator—a newly created position.

sentences.zh: 斯得分修光、寧二帝《紀》。

translations.literal: Side was assigned to compile the Annals of the Guang and Ning emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Side was assigned to compile the annals of Emperors Guangzong and Ningzong.

sentences.zh: 尋遷史館校勘，又遷軍器監主簿兼史館校勘。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to History Institute collator, then to chief clerk of the Armory Directorate, concurrently History Institute collator.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made History Institute collator, then chief clerk of the Armory Directorate while retaining his post as History Institute collator.

sentences.zh: 時丞相史嵩之柄國，斯得遇對，空臆盡言。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Councillor Shi Songzhi held state power; when Side had audience he emptied his breast and spoke fully.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Shi Songzhi then held state power. When Side had audience, he spoke his mind without reserve.

sentences.zh: 冬雷，斯得應詔上封事，乞擇才並相，由是迕嵩之意。

translations.literal: Winter thunder—Side responded to the edict with a sealed memorial begging to select talent and share the chief ministership; thereby he offended Song's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When winter thunder struck, Side submitted a sealed memorial in response to the edict, urging the selection of talent to share the chief ministership, thereby offending Songzhi.

sentences.zh: 遷太常寺主簿，仍兼史館校勘。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, still concurrently History Institute collator.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while retaining his post as History Institute collator.

sentences.zh: 時斯得叔父定子以禮部尚書領史事，時人以為美談。

translations.literal: At the time Side's uncle Dingzi as Minister of Rites led historical affairs—people of the time regarded it as a fine story.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his uncle Gao Dingzi, as Minister of Rites, directed historical affairs—a pairing much admired at court.

sentences.zh: 會太學博士劉應起入對，拄嵩之，嵩之恚，使其黨言叔父兄子不可同朝，以斯得添差通判紹興府。

translations.literal: It happened that Imperial Academy erudite Liu Yingqi entered audience and impeached Songzhi; Songzhi was enraged and had his faction say uncle and nephew could not serve in court together, and Side was given an added assignment as vice prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Imperial Academy erudite Liu Yingqi memorialized against Songzhi at audience, Songzhi was enraged and had his faction argue that uncle and nephew could not serve together. Side was given an added assignment as vice prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 淳祐二年，四朝《帝紀》書成，上之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunyou the Imperial Annals of four reigns were completed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1242 the Imperial Annals of four reigns were completed and submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 嵩之妄加毀譽於理宗、濟王，改斯得所草《寧宗紀》末卷，斯得與史官杜範、王遂辨之。

translations.literal: Songzhi recklessly added praise and blame regarding Emperor Lizong and Prince Ji, altering the final fascicle of the Ningzong Annals that Side had drafted; Side with historians Du Fan and Wang Sui disputed it.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi arbitrarily inserted praise and blame regarding Emperor Lizong and Prince Ji, altering the final fascicle of the Ningzong Annals that Side had drafted. Side disputed this with historians Du Fan and Wang Sui.

sentences.zh: 範報書亦有“奸人剿入邪說”之語，然書已登進矣。

translations.literal: Fan's reply letter also had the words "villains have smuggled in heterodox doctrines," but the book had already been submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's reply also spoke of "villains smuggling in heterodox doctrines," but the altered text had already been submitted.

sentences.zh: 心傳藏斯得所草，題其末曰“前史官高某撰”而已。

translations.literal: Xinchuan preserved what Side had drafted and at the end inscribed only "Drafted by former historian Gao so-and-so."
translations.idiomatic: Xinchuan preserved Side's draft and inscribed at the end only, "Drafted by former historian Gao."

sentences.zh: 逾年，添差通判台州。

translations.literal: After a year he was given an added assignment as vice prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he received an added assignment as vice prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 範既入相，召為太常博士，遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: When Fan had entered the chief ministership, Side was summoned as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transferred to Secretariat gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fan became chief minister, Side was summoned as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to Secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 六年正月朔，日有食之，斯得應詔上封事，言：“大奸嗜權，巧營奪服，陛下奮獨斷而罷退之，是矣。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the sixth year there was an eclipse of the sun; Side responded to the edict with a sealed memorial saying, "The great villain craves power and craftily schemes to seize mourning garb; Your Majesty exerted independent judgment and dismissed him—this was right."
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the sixth year there was a solar eclipse. Side submitted a sealed memorial saying, "The great villain craved power and craftily schemed to seize control during mourning. Your Majesty acted with independent judgment and dismissed him—that was right."

sentences.zh: 諫憲之臣，交疏其惡，或請投之荒裔，或請勒之休致。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and surveillance officials jointly memorialized his crimes, some begging to cast him into remote regions, some begging to compel his retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and surveillance officials jointly exposed his crimes, some urging exile to remote regions, others demanding forced retirement.

sentences.zh: 陛下苟行其言，亦足昭示意向，渙釋群疑。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty had carried out their words, it would also have sufficed to display intent and dissolve the crowd's doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Had Your Majesty acted on their advice, it would have sufficed to clarify your intent and dispel public doubts.

sentences.zh: 乃一切寢而不宣，曆時既久，人言不置，然後黽勉傳諭，委曲誨奸，俾於襲絰之時，妄致掛冠之請，因降祠命，苟塞人言，又有奸人陰為之地。

translations.literal: Yet everything was shelved and not proclaimed; time passed long and people's words did not cease; only then with effort was instruction transmitted, tactfully admonishing the villain, enabling him during the wearing of unhemmed sackcloth falsely to offer to hang up his cap, and thereby a temple appointment was granted to perfunctorily stop people's words—moreover villains secretly made room for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet everything was shelved and kept quiet. As time passed and public criticism did not cease, the court reluctantly issued instructions, tactfully indulging the villain until, during the mourning period, he falsely offered to resign, whereupon a temple appointment was granted merely to silence criticism—while villains secretly paved his way back.

sentences.zh: 是以訛言並興，善類解體，謂聖意之難測，而大奸之必還，莽、卓、操、懿之禍，將有不忍言者。

translations.literal: Therefore false reports arose together, good men dissolved in dismay, saying the sage intent was hard to fathom and the great villain would surely return—the calamities of Mang, Zhuo, Cao, and Yi would have what cannot be borne to speak.
translations.idiomatic: False rumors spread, good men lost heart, and people said the sovereign's intent was unfathomable while the great villain would surely return—the catastrophes of Wang Mang, Dong Zhuo, Cao Cao, and Sima Yi would be unbearable to contemplate.

sentences.zh: ”時監察御史江萬里及它台諫累疏論嵩之罪惡，竟不施行，第因嵩之致仕，予祠而已，故斯得封事首及之。

translations.literal: " At the time Surveillance Censor Jiang Wanli and other remonstrance officials repeatedly memorialized on Songzhi's crimes, yet nothing was carried out—only because Songzhi retired was a temple post granted; therefore Side's sealed memorial first addressed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Surveillance Censor Jiang Wanli and other remonstrance officials had repeatedly memorialized on Songzhi's crimes, yet nothing was done—only a temple appointment when he retired. Side's sealed memorial addressed this first.

sentences.zh: 又言：“大臣貴乎以道事君，今乃獻替之義少而容悅之意多，知恥之念輕而患失之心重。

translations.literal: He also said, "Great ministers are valued for serving the ruler by the Way; now the meaning of offering and replacing is little while the intent to please appearance is much; the thought of shame is light while the heart of fearing loss is heavy."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Great ministers should serve the ruler by the Way. Today they offer little candid counsel and much flattery; they feel little shame and fear losing office above all."

sentences.zh: 內降當執奏，則不待下殿而已行；

translations.literal: when inner edicts should be firmly memorialized, they are carried out without waiting to leave the hall;
translations.idiomatic: When inner edicts should be firmly memorialized against, they are implemented before the minister even leaves the hall;

sentences.zh: 濫恩當裁抑，則不從中覆而遽命。

translations.literal: when excessive favor should be restrained, orders are hurried without awaiting central review.
translations.idiomatic: when excessive favors should be restrained, orders are rushed through without awaiting central review.

sentences.zh: 嫉正而庇邪，喜同而惡異，任術而詭道，樂俞而憚勞。

translations.literal: They hate the upright and shelter the wicked, delight in agreement and hate difference, employ craft and pervert the Way, rejoice in assent and dread labor.
translations.idiomatic: They hate the upright and shelter the wicked, favor agreement and despise dissent, rely on craft rather than principle, and welcome flattery while dreading hard work.

sentences.zh: 陛下虛心委寄，所責者何事，而其應乃爾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty with open mind has entrusted them—what is entrusted, and yet their response is thus.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has entrusted them with open confidence—yet this is how they respond to what you charge them with.

sentences.zh: ”時範鍾獨當國，過失日章，故斯得及之。

translations.literal: " At the time Fan and Zhong alone held the state; faults daily became manifest—therefore Side addressed them.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Fan and Zhong alone governed the state, and their faults grew daily more evident—therefore Side addressed them.

sentences.zh: 又言：“便嬖側媚之人，尤足為清明之累，腐夫巧讒而使傳幾搖，妖監外通而魁邪密主，陰奸伏蠱，互煽交攻，陛下之心至是其存者幾希矣。

translations.literal: He also said, "Favorites and flatterers are especially able to burden clarity; corrupt men craftily slander so that transmission nearly shakes; demon eunuchs connect outside while chief villains secretly hold mastery; hidden villains lie in wait like gu poison, mutually fanning and attacking each other—Your Majesty's heart by then has scarcely anything left."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Favorites and flatterers are especially damaging to clear governance. Corrupt men craft slanders that nearly shake the realm; eunuchs collude with outsiders while chief villains hold secret sway. Hidden villains lie in wait, fanning one another's attacks—by then Your Majesty's heart retains scarcely anything of its former clarity."

sentences.zh: 陛下之心，大化之本也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heart is the root of great transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's heart is the root of great transformation.

sentences.zh: 洗濯磨淬，思所以更之，乃徒立為虛言無實之名，而謂之更化，此天心之所以未當，大異之所以示儆也。

translations.literal: Wash and polish, grind and temper, think how to change it—yet you merely establish empty names without substance and call it renewal of transformation; this is why heaven's heart is not satisfied and great anomalies show warning.
translations.idiomatic: You should wash and polish your heart, thinking how to renew it—yet you merely proclaim empty names without substance and call it renewal. This is why heaven's heart is not satisfied and great portents warn you.

sentences.zh: ”言尤切直，帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: " His words were especially cutting and direct; the emperor praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: " His words were especially blunt and direct, and the emperor commended and accepted them.

sentences.zh: 又言：“群臣厖雜，宮禁奇邪，黷貨外交，豈可坐視而不之問！

translations.literal: He also said, "The hundred officials are numerous and mixed, the palace forbidden holds strange perversity, corrupt goods connect outside—how can one sit and watch without inquiring!"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Officials are numerous and corrupt, the palace harbors strange perversities, and illicit trade reaches beyond the court—how can you sit and watch without investigating!"

sentences.zh: 顧乃並包兼容之意多，別邪辨正之慮淺，憂讒避謗之心重，直前邁往之誌微，遂使眾臣爭衡，大權旁落，養成積輕之勢，以開窺覬之漸。

translations.literal: Yet the intent to embrace and tolerate is much, the thought to distinguish evil and discern right is shallow, the heart to fear slander and avoid calumny is heavy, the will to press straight forward is slight—thus the many ministers contend for balance, great power falls to the side, a momentum of accumulated lightness is nurtured, and the first steps of covetous watching are opened.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you embrace and tolerate too much, distinguish evil from right too little, fear slander too greatly, and press forward too little—so ministers contend for power, authority slips away, contempt accumulates, and the first steps toward usurpation are opened.

sentences.zh: 設有不幸，變故乘之，上心一移，凶渠立至，使宗社有淪亡之憂，衣冠遭魚肉之禍，生靈罹塗炭之厄。

translations.literal: If misfortune occurs and change rides upon it, the upper heart shifts once and the villainous ringleader immediately arrives, making the altars of state face the worry of ruin, the gentry and officials suffer the calamity of being carved like fish and meat, and the living people encounter the ordeal of charcoal and mud.
translations.idiomatic: If misfortune strikes and crisis follows, once the sovereign's heart wavers the villainous ringleader will appear at once, bringing the altars of state to ruin, the gentry to slaughter, and the people to misery.

sentences.zh: 當是時也，能潔身以去，其能逃萬世之清議乎？

translations.literal: At that time, can one who could purify his person and depart escape the clear judgment of ten thousand ages?
translations.idiomatic: At that time, could one who failed to withdraw with integrity escape the judgment of posterity?

sentences.zh: ”於是群憸悚懼，或泣訴上前，或上章求去，合力排擯，斯得遂求補外。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the villainous group were fearful, some weeping and appealing before the throne, some submitting memorials begging to leave, combining strength to ostracize him, and Side then begged for an outer appointment.
translations.idiomatic: " The villainous faction grew fearful; some wept before the throne, others submitted resignations, and together they ostracized him until Side sought an appointment outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 在告幾百餘日，於是差知嚴州，斯得三請乞祠，不許。

translations.literal: On leave for nearly a hundred days, he was then assigned as magistrate of Yanzhou; Side three times begged for a temple post—not granted.
translations.idiomatic: After nearly a hundred days on leave, he was assigned magistrate of Yanzhou. Side three times begged for a temple appointment; each request was denied.

sentences.zh: 嚴環山為郡，雖豐歲猶仰它州。

translations.literal: Yan is a prefecture ringed by mountains; even in abundant years it still relies on other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou is a mountain-ringed prefecture that even in good years depends on other prefectures for grain.

sentences.zh: 夏旱，斯得蠲租發廩，招糴勸分，請於朝，得米萬石以振濟。

translations.literal: Summer drought—Side remitted rent and opened granaries, recruited grain purchase and urged sharing, requested from court, and obtained ten thousand shi of rice for relief.
translations.idiomatic: During a summer drought, Side remitted rents, opened granaries, organized grain purchases, and urged mutual aid. He requested aid from court and obtained ten thousand shi of rice for relief.

sentences.zh: 遷浙東提點刑獄，遂劾知處州趙善瀚、知台州沈暨等七人倚勢厲民，疏上，不報。

translations.literal: He was transferred to judicial intendant of Eastern Zhe, then impeached Zhao Shanhui, prefect of Chuzhou, Shen Ji, prefect of Taizhou, and five others for relying on power to oppress the people; the memorial was submitted—no response.
translations.idiomatic: He was made judicial intendant of Eastern Zhe and impeached Zhao Shanhui of Chuzhou, Shen Ji of Taizhou, and five others for abusing power to oppress the people. His memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 改江西轉運判官，斯得具辭免，上奏曰：“臣劾奏趙善瀚等七人，未聞報可，固疑必有黨與營救，惑誤聖聽，今奉恩除，乃知中臣所料。

translations.literal: Changed to Jiangxi transport vice commissioner, Side fully declined and submitted: "Your servant impeached Zhao Shanhui and seven others; no approval was heard—I firmly suspected there must be factional rescue misleading the sage hearing; now receiving gracious appointment, I know I hit the mark."
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Jiangxi transport vice commissioner. Side fully declined and memorialized: "I impeached Zhao Shanhui and seven others but heard no approval, suspecting factional rescue had misled Your Majesty. Now that I receive this gracious appointment, I know my suspicions were correct."

sentences.zh: 善瀚者，侍御史周坦之婦翁也，贓吏之魁，錮於聖世，鄭清之與之有舊，復與州符。

translations.literal: Shanhui is the father-in-law of Attending Censor Zhou Tan, chief of corrupt officials, confined in the sage age; Zheng Qingzhi had old ties with him and again gave him a prefectural commission.
translations.idiomatic: Shanhui is the father-in-law of Attending Censor Zhou Tan, a leading corrupt official who should have been barred from office. Zheng Qingzhi, who had old ties with him, restored him to a prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 沈塈者，同簽書樞密院事史宅之妻黨也。

translations.literal: Shen Ji is a relative by marriage of Co-signing Secretary Shi Zhai of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ji is related by marriage to Co-signing Secretary Shi Zhai of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 祖宗以來，未有監司按吏一不施行者，壞法亂紀，未有甚此。

translations.literal: Since the ancestors, there has never been a case where a surveillance commissioner impeached an official and not one was carried out—to destroy law and disorder discipline, nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the dynasty, no surveillance commissioner's impeachment has ever gone entirely unenforced. Nothing has so thoroughly destroyed law and discipline as this.

sentences.zh: 臣身為使者，劾吏不行，反叨易節，若貪榮冒拜，則與世之頑頓無恥者何異？

translations.literal: Your servant as envoy—impeachment not carried out, yet receiving a change of commission—if greedy for glory and rashly accepting, how is this different from the stubborn shameless of the world?
translations.idiomatic: As an envoy whose impeachment went unenforced, to accept a new commission would be no different from the shameless opportunists of the age.

sentences.zh: 乞並臣鐫罷，以戒奉使無狀者。

translations.literal: I beg that your servant also be struck and dismissed, to warn envoys who behave without propriety.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that I too be dismissed, to warn envoys who behave without propriety.

sentences.zh: ”章既上，坦自謂己任台諫而反見攻，遍懇同列論斯得，同列難之，計急，自上章劾罷斯得新任，未幾，坦亦罷，七人竟罷去。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, Tan thought himself charged with remonstrance yet was instead attacked; he broadly begged colleagues to discuss Side; colleagues found it difficult; plan urgent—he himself submitted a memorial impeaching and dismissing Side's new appointment; before long Tan was also dismissed, and the seven were finally dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, Tan, who held a remonstrance post, felt himself attacked and urgently pressed colleagues to act against Side. Finding little support, he memorialized to block Side's new appointment. Soon Tan himself was dismissed, and all seven corrupt officials were finally removed.

sentences.zh: 移湖南提點刑獄，薦通判潭州徐經孫等六人。

translations.literal: Transferred to judicial intendant of Hunan, he recommended Vice Prefect of Tanzhou Xu Jingsun and five others.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to judicial intendant of Hunan and recommended Vice Prefect of Tanzhou Xu Jingsun and five others.

sentences.zh: 攸懸富民陳衡老，以家丁糧食資強賊，劫殺平民。

translations.literal: In Youxian, wealthy man Chen Henglao used household servants' grain and food to supply strong bandits, robbing and killing common people.
translations.idiomatic: In Youxian, the wealthy Chen Henglao used his household servants' grain to supply bandits who robbed and killed commoners.

sentences.zh: 斯得至，有訴其事者，首吏受賕而左右之，衡老造庭，首吏拱立。

translations.literal: When Side arrived, someone complained of the matter; the chief clerk took bribes and favored him; Henglao came to the hall and the chief clerk stood with folded hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Side arrived, someone lodged a complaint. The chief clerk had taken bribes and favored Henglao, who came to the hall while the clerk stood deferentially by.

sentences.zh: 斯得發其奸，械首吏下獄，群胥失色股栗。

translations.literal: Side exposed his villainy, shackled the chief clerk and sent him to prison; the host of clerks lost color and trembled in their legs.
translations.idiomatic: Side exposed the crime, shackled the chief clerk, and sent him to prison. The other clerks turned pale and trembled.

sentences.zh: 於是研鞫具得其狀，乃黥配首吏，具白朝省，追毀衡老官資，簿錄其家。

translations.literal: Thereupon through investigation and interrogation the full circumstances were obtained; the chief clerk was tattooed and banished; fully reported to the court and provinces; Henglao's official credentials were pursued and destroyed, and his household was inventoried.
translations.idiomatic: Through investigation the full facts emerged. The chief clerk was tattooed and banished. Side reported to the central government, stripped Henglao of his official rank, and inventoried his property.

sentences.zh: 會諸邑水災，衡老願出米五萬石振濟以贖罪。

translations.literal: It happened that various districts had flood disaster; Henglao wished to offer fifty thousand shi of rice for relief to redeem his crime.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck the region, Henglao offered fifty thousand shi of rice for relief to redeem his crimes.

sentences.zh: 衡老婿吳自性，與衡老館客太學生馮煒等謀中傷斯得盜拆官櫝。

translations.literal: Henglao's son-in-law Wu Zixing, with Henglao's lodge guest Imperial Academy student Feng Wei and others, plotted to slander Side for stealing and breaking open official coffers.
translations.idiomatic: Henglao's son-in-law Wu Zixing, with lodge guest and Imperial Academy student Feng Wei and others, plotted to slander Side for stealing and breaking open official coffers.

sentences.zh: 斯得白於朝，復正其罪，出一篋書，具得自性等交通省部吏胥情狀。

translations.literal: Side reported to court, again established their crimes, and produced a box of documents fully obtaining the circumstances of Zixing and others connecting with provincial ministry clerks and runners.
translations.idiomatic: Side reported to court, re-established their guilt, and produced a box of documents detailing how Zixing and others had bribed central government clerks.

sentences.zh: 斯得並言於朝，下其事天府，索出賕銀六萬餘兩，黥配自性及省寺高鑄等二十餘人。

translations.literal: Side also reported to court; the matter was sent down to the metropolitan office; more than sixty thousand liang of bribe silver was sought out; Zixing and provincial temple Gao Zhu and more than twenty others were tattooed and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Side reported further to court. The case was referred to the metropolitan office, which uncovered more than sixty thousand liang in bribes. Zixing, Gao Zhu, and more than twenty others were tattooed and banished.

sentences.zh: 初，自性厚賂宦者言於理宗曰：“斯得以緡錢百萬進，願易近地一節。

translations.literal: Earlier Zixing had richly bribed eunuchs to say to Emperor Lizong, "Side offered a million strings of cash in bribes, wishing to exchange for a nearby post."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zixing had bribed eunuchs to tell Emperor Lizong, "Side offered a million strings of cash in bribes, seeking a post nearer the capital."

sentences.zh: ”理宗曰：“高某硬漢，安得有是。

translations.literal: " Lizong said, "Gao is a hard man—how could there be such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: " Lizong said, "Gao is a hard man—how could he do such a thing?"

sentences.zh: ”而斯得力求去，清之以書留之。

translations.literal: " Yet Side forcefully begged to leave; Qingzhi with a letter detained him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet Side pressed to resign, and Qingzhi wrote to detain him.

sentences.zh: 又薦李晞顏等五人。

translations.literal: He also recommended Li Xiyan and five others.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Li Xiyan and five others.

sentences.zh: 加直秘閣、湖南轉運判官，改尚右郎官，未至，改禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He was added as Direct Attendant of the Secret Repository and Hunan transport vice commissioner, changed to Right Gentleman of the Ministry of Works; before arriving, changed to Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Direct Attendant of the Secret Repository and Hunan transport vice commissioner, then Right Gentleman of the Ministry of Works; before he could take up the post, he was made Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 上疏極論時事，改權左司，力辭，內批兼侍立修注官。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial exhaustively discussing current affairs, was changed to Acting Left Director, forcefully declined, and received an inner endorsement to concurrently attend in attendance and compile annotations.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized at length on current affairs, was offered Acting Left Director, declined forcefully, and received an inner endorsement to concurrently attend court and compile annotations.

sentences.zh: 言水災曰：“願陛下立罷新寺土木，速反迕旨諸臣，遏絕邪說，主張善良，謹重刑辟，愛惜士類，抑遠佞臣，絕其幹撓，則天意可回，和氣可召矣。

translations.literal: Speaking of flood disaster he said, "I wish Your Majesty immediately to stop new temple earthworks, quickly reverse the ministers who defy edicts, check and end heterodox doctrines, uphold the good and kind, carefully respect punishments, cherish the scholarly class, suppress and distance flatterers, cut off their interference—then heaven's intent can turn back and harmonious qi can be summoned."
translations.idiomatic: On the floods he said, "I urge Your Majesty to halt new temple construction at once, recall ministers who defy your edicts, suppress heterodox doctrines, uphold the good, respect the law, cherish scholars, keep flatterers at a distance and end their interference—then heaven's favor may return and harmony be restored."

sentences.zh: ”會斥左司徐霖，帝慮給事中趙汝騰爭逐霖事，乃徙汝騰翰林學士，汝騰聞命即去國。

translations.literal: " It happened that Left Director Xu Lin was dismissed; the emperor feared Supervising Secretary Zhao Ruteng would dispute expelling Lin and therefore transferred Ruteng to Hanlin Academician; Ruteng on hearing the order immediately left the state.
translations.idiomatic: " When Left Director Xu Lin was dismissed, the emperor feared Supervising Secretary Zhao Ruteng would dispute the matter and transferred him to Hanlin Academician. Ruteng left the capital immediately on receiving the order.

sentences.zh: 斯得言：“汝騰一世之望，宗老之重，飄然引去，陛下遂亦棄之有如弁髦，中外驚怪，將見賢者力爭不勝而去，小人踴躍增氣而來。

translations.literal: Side said, "Ruteng is the hope of an age, the weight of the clan elders—he drifted away and departed; Your Majesty then also abandoned him like a cap tassel; inside and outside were startled and amazed; one will see worthies striving in force yet not prevailing and departing, while petty men leap with added spirit and come."
translations.idiomatic: Side said, "Ruteng is the hope of the age, a pillar of the elder statesmen—yet he departed at once, and Your Majesty cast him aside like a discarded cap tassel. Court and country were astonished. Worthies will strive in vain and leave, while petty men will leap forward with renewed confidence."

sentences.zh: 陛下改紀僅數月，初意遽變，臣深惜之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's renewal of rule has been only a few months, yet the original intent suddenly changed—your servant deeply regrets it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's renewal of rule has lasted only a few months, yet the original intent has suddenly shifted—I deeply regret this.

sentences.zh: 時上封事言得失者眾，或者惡其讙詉，遂謂“空言徒亂人聽，無補國事。

translations.literal: At the time many submitted sealed memorials on gains and losses; some hated the clamor and thus said, "Empty words only disturb people's hearing and do not aid state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Many were submitting sealed memorials on policy. Some resented the clamor and said, "Empty words only confuse listeners and do nothing for state affairs."

sentences.zh: ”斯得因轉對，言：“諸臣之言，上則切劘聖主，下則砥礪大臣，內則摧壓奸邪，外則銷遏寇虐，顧以為無補於實政乎？

translations.literal: " Side on rotating audience said, "The words of the various ministers above cut and sharpen the sage ruler, below grind and hone great ministers, within crush and press villainy, outside dissolve and check bandit cruelty—yet you think they do not aid real governance?"
translations.idiomatic: " At rotating audience Side said, "Ministers' words sharpen the ruler above, hone ministers below, suppress villainy within, and check enemies without—yet you call them useless to governance?"

sentences.zh: 空言之譏，好名之說，欲一網君子而盡去之，其言易入，其禍難言，此君子去留之機，國家安危之候，不可不深留聖慮者也。

translations.literal: The ridicule of empty words, the talk of loving fame, wishing to net gentlemen in one sweep and remove them all—their words enter easily, their calamity is hard to speak; this is the hinge of gentlemen's going and staying, the sign of the state's safety and peril—it cannot but deeply retain the sage consideration.
translations.idiomatic: The charge of empty words, the accusation of seeking fame—the wish to net all gentlemen and drive them out—these words are easily believed, but their harm is incalculable. This is the hinge on which gentlemen stay or go and the state stands or falls. Your Majesty must ponder it deeply.

sentences.zh: ”監察御史蕭泰來論罷。

translations.literal: " Surveillance Censor Xiao Tailai was impeached and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " Surveillance Censor Xiao Tailai was impeached and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以直寶文閣知泉州，力辭，遷福建路計度轉運副使。

translations.literal: After a year, as Direct Attendant of the Baowen Pavilion he was made prefect of Quanzhou; he forcefully declined and was transferred to Fujian Circuit vice commissioner of fiscal planning and transport.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made Direct Attendant of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Quanzhou. He declined forcefully and was transferred to Fujian Circuit vice commissioner of fiscal planning and transport.

sentences.zh: 朝廷行自實田，斯得言：“按《史記》，秦始皇三十一年，令民自實田。

translations.literal: The court implemented self-reporting of fields; Side said, "According to the Records of the Grand Historian, in the thirty-first year of Qin Shihuang he ordered the people to self-report their fields."
translations.idiomatic: When the court implemented self-reporting of landholdings, Side said, "According to the Records of the Grand Historian, in the thirty-first year of his reign Qin Shihuang ordered the people to self-report their fields."

sentences.zh: 主上臨禦適三十一年，而異日書之史冊，自實之名正與秦同。

translations.literal: Our ruler's facing the realm happens to be exactly thirty-one years, yet when written in the historical records another day, the name self-reporting is exactly the same as Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned exactly thirty-one years, yet when this is recorded in history, the name 'self-reporting' will be identical to Qin's policy.

sentences.zh: ”丞相謝方叔大愧，即為之罷。

translations.literal: " Chief Councillor Xie Fangshu was greatly ashamed and immediately abolished it for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Councillor Xie Fangshu was deeply shamed and immediately abolished the policy.

sentences.zh: 董槐入相，召為司農卿。

translations.literal: Dong Huai entered the chief ministership and summoned him as Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Huai became chief minister, Side was summoned as Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 程元鳳入相，改秘書監。

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanfeng entered the chief ministership and he was changed to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Yuanfeng became chief minister, Side was made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁大全入相，監察御史沈炎論斯得以閩漕交承錢物，下郡吏天府，榜死數人。

translations.literal: Ding Daquan entered the chief ministership; Surveillance Censor Shen Yan impeached Side for Fujian transport handover of money and goods; county clerks were sent down to the metropolitan office; several died under beating.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Daquan became chief minister, Surveillance Censor Shen Yan impeached Side for mishandling Fujian transport funds. The case was referred to the metropolitan office, and several clerks died under interrogation.

sentences.zh: 先是，吳自性之獄，高鑄為首惡黥配廣州，捐資免行，至是為相府監奴，嗾炎發其端。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Wu Zixing's case, Gao Zhu as chief villain was tattooed and banished to Guangzhou; he donated funds to avoid going; by this time he was a supervising slave in the chief minister's mansion and instigated Yan to launch the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Wu Zixing's case, Gao Zhu had been tattooed and banished to Guangzhou but bought his way out of exile. By now he was a supervised bondsman in the chief minister's mansion and instigated Yan to launch the case.

sentences.zh: 京尹顧岩傅會其獄，安吉守何夢然奉行其事，陵鑠甚至，斯得不少挫，竟無所得。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Magistrate Gu Yan joined the case; Anji Defender He Mengran carried out the matter; oppression was extreme; Side was not slightly broken—and in the end nothing was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Magistrate Gu Yan joined the prosecution, and Anji Defender He Mengran carried it out with extreme harshness. Side was not broken, and in the end they found nothing.

sentences.zh: 大全既謫，朝廷罪其委任非人，遂斬鑄。

translations.literal: When Daquan was demoted, the court blamed him for entrusting unfit persons and then executed Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: After Daquan was demoted, the court blamed him for appointing unfit men and executed Zhu.

sentences.zh: 斯得既拜浙西提點刑獄之命，炎，浙西人，泣於上前，乞更之，移浙東提舉常平。

translations.literal: When Side had received appointment as judicial intendant of Western Zhe, Yan—a man of Western Zhe—wept before the throne begging to change it; he was moved to Eastern Zhe intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Side was appointed judicial intendant of Western Zhe, Yan—a native of Western Zhe—wept before the throne begging a different assignment and was transferred to Eastern Zhe intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 命下，給事中章鑒繳還。
