translations.literal: When the order was issued, Supervising Secretary Zhang Jian returned it withheld.
translations.idiomatic: When the order was issued, Supervising Secretary Zhang Jian returned it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 斯得杜門不出，著《孝宗係年要錄》。

translations.literal: Side closed his doors and did not go out, composing the Essential Annals by Year of Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Side shut his doors and wrote the Essential Annals by Year of Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 彗星見，應詔上封事，曰：“陛下專任一相，虛心委之，果得其人，宜天心克享，災害不生。

translations.literal: A comet appeared; responding to the edict he submitted a sealed memorial saying, "Your Majesty exclusively employs one chief minister and with open mind entrusts him—if you truly obtain the right man, heaven's heart should be satisfied and disasters should not arise."
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared, he submitted a sealed memorial saying, "Your Majesty entrusts all power to a single chief minister. If you have chosen the right man, heaven should be satisfied and disasters should not arise."

sentences.zh: 而庚申、己未之歲，大水為災，浙西之民死者數百千萬。

translations.literal: Yet in the gengshen and jiwei years great floods became disaster; the people of Western Zhe who died numbered several millions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in those years great floods struck, and millions died in Western Zhe.

sentences.zh: 連年旱暵，田野蕭條，物價翔躍，民命如線。

translations.literal: Years of drought; fields desolate; prices soaring; people's lives like threads.
translations.idiomatic: Years of drought left the fields desolate, prices soared, and people's lives hung by a thread.

sentences.zh: 今妖星突出，其變不小。

translations.literal: Now the demon star protrudes—its change is not small.
translations.idiomatic: Now a comet has appeared—its portent is grave.

sentences.zh: 若非大失人心，何以致天怒如此之烈。

translations.literal: If not for greatly losing the people's hearts, how could heaven's anger be so fierce?
translations.idiomatic: If the court had not gravely lost the people's hearts, how could heaven's wrath be so fierce?

sentences.zh: ”封事之上也，似道匿不以聞。

translations.literal: " When the sealed memorial was submitted, Jia Sidao concealed it and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: " When the sealed memorial was submitted, Jia Sidao suppressed it and did not report it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 台諫徐直方等四人論似道誤國之罪，乞安置嶺表，簿錄其家。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Xu Zhifang and four others discussed Jia Sidao's crime of misleading the state, begging to settle him in the Lingnan region and inventory his household.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials Xu Zhifang and four others charged Jia Sidao with misleading the state, urging exile to the far south and confiscation of his property.

sentences.zh: 丞相留夢炎庇護似道，止令散官居住，且謂簿錄擾及無辜。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Liu Mengyan sheltered Sidao, only ordering him to reside as a dismissed official, and said inventorying would disturb the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Liu Mengyan shielded Sidao, merely ordering him to live in retirement as a dismissed official, and argued that confiscation would harm the innocent.

sentences.zh: 斯得謂“散官則安置，追降官分司則居住，祖宗製也。

translations.literal: Side said, "Dismissed officials are settled in exile; demoted officials on branch duty reside—this is ancestral regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Side said, "Dismissed officials are exiled; demoted officials on branch duty merely reside at home—that is ancestral law."

sentences.zh: ”夢炎語塞。

translations.literal: " Mengyan was speechless.
translations.idiomatic: " Mengyan had no reply.

sentences.zh: 夢炎乘間直罷去平章事王鑰、監察御史俞浙，並罷斯得，於是宋亡矣。

translations.literal: Mengyan seized an interval and directly dismissed Grand Councillor Wang Yue and Surveillance Censor Yu Zhe, and also dismissed Side—thereupon Song perished.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyan seized an opportunity to dismiss Grand Councillor Wang Yue and Surveillance Censor Yu Zhe, and also dismissed Side—and with that the Song fell.

sentences.zh: 所著有《詩膚說》、《儀禮合抄》、《增損刊正杜佑通典》、《徽宗長編》、《孝宗係年要錄》、《恥堂文集》行世。

translations.literal: Works in circulation include Exposition on the Skin of Poetry, Combined Copy of the Ceremonies, Augmented and Corrected Du You's Comprehensive Institutions, Long Compilation of Huizong, Essential Annals by Year of Xiaozong, and Collected Writings from the Hall of Shame.
translations.idiomatic: His works in circulation include Exposition on the Skin of Poetry, Combined Copy of the Ceremonies, his revised edition of Du You's Comprehensive Institutions, the Long Compilation of Huizong, the Essential Annals by Year of Xiaozong, and the Collected Writings from the Hall of Shame.

sentences.zh: 張忠恕，字行父，右仆射浚之孫。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongshu, courtesy name Xingfu, was the grandson of Right Vice Director Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongshu, styled Xingfu, was the grandson of Right Vice Director Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 以祖任，監樓店務。

translations.literal: Through his grandfather's privilege he supervised the tower shop office.
translations.idiomatic: Through his grandfather's privilege he supervised the tower shop office.

sentences.zh: 入府幕，時韓侂胄權勢熏灼，嚐奪民間已許嫁女，夫家以告，忠恕白尹歸其父母，尹不能難。

translations.literal: He entered the prefectural staff; at the time Han Tuozhou's power blazed; he once seized a commoner's daughter already betrothed; the groom's family complained; Zhongshu told the prefect to return her to her parents—the prefect could not object.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the prefectural staff when Han Tuozhou's power was at its height. Tuozhou once seized a commoner's daughter already betrothed. When the groom's family complained, Zhongshu persuaded the prefect to return her to her parents, and the prefect could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 再調廣西轉運司主管文字，改通判沅州，主管京湖宣撫司機宜文字，知澧州。

translations.literal: Again transferred as chief clerk for texts of Guangxi transport commission, changed to vice prefect of Yuanzhou, in charge of opportune documents for the Jing-Hu Pacification Office, and magistrate of Li Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk for texts in the Guangxi transport commission, then made vice prefect of Yuanzhou, handler of documents for the Jing-Hu Pacification Office, and magistrate of Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開禧末，入為籍田令。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaixi he entered service as Director of the Sacred Field.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaixi era he was appointed Director of the Sacred Field.

sentences.zh: 屬太廟鴟吻為雷雨壞，神主遷禦，忠恕因輪對，請廣言路，通下情，寧宗嘉納。

translations.literal: When the ancestral temple's ridge ornaments were damaged by thunder and rain and the spirit tablets were moved for protection, Zhongshu on rotating audience begged to broaden the path of speech and communicate lower sentiments; Ningzong praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When thunder damaged the ancestral temple's roof ornaments and the spirit tablets were moved for safekeeping, Zhongshu at rotating audience urged broadening the path of remonstrance and communicating the people's sentiments. Ningzong commended and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 嘉定五年，遷軍器丞，進太府丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiading he was transferred to Vice Director of the Armory and advanced to Vice Director of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In 1212 he was made Vice Director of the Armory and promoted to Vice Director of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 出知湖州。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷司農丞、知寧國府。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Director of Agriculture and magistrate of Ningguo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of Agriculture and magistrate of Ningguo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 夏旱，請於朝，得賜僧牒五十，米十萬七千餘石。

translations.literal: Summer drought—he requested from court and obtained fifty monk certificates and more than one hundred seven thousand shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: During a summer drought he requested aid from court and received fifty monk certificates and more than 107,000 shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 常平使者欲均濟而勿勸糶，忠恕慮後無以濟，遂核戶口、計歲月，嚴戒諸邑諭大家發蓋藏。

translations.literal: The Ever-Normal envoy wished to equalize relief but not urge sale of grain; Zhongshu feared later there would be no means of relief, so he checked household registers and calculated months, strictly warning the districts to instruct great families to release stored grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Ever-Normal envoy wished to distribute relief but not encourage grain sales. Zhongshu feared there would be nothing left for later needs, so he checked household registers, calculated the months ahead, and strictly ordered the districts to persuade wealthy families to release their stored grain.

sentences.zh: 所見浸異，以言去，主管衝佑觀。

translations.literal: What he saw gradually differed; he left on account of his words and supervised the Chongyou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: His views increasingly diverged from those around him; he resigned over his remonstrance and supervised the Chongyou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 起知鄂州，改湖北轉運判官兼知鄂州。

translations.literal: He was raised to magistrate of Ezhou, then changed to Hubei transport vice commissioner concurrently magistrate of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as magistrate of Ezhou, then made Hubei transport vice commissioner while retaining the Ezhou post.

sentences.zh: 召為屯田郎官，丁內艱。

translations.literal: Summoned as Gentleman of the Directorate of Domains; he mourned an inner bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Gentleman of the Directorate of Domains but mourned a close relative.

sentences.zh: 免喪，入為戶部郎官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he entered as Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he entered service as Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 入對，極言邊事，其慮至遠。

translations.literal: Entering audience he spoke to the utmost on border affairs; his concerns reached very far.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he spoke at length on border affairs with far-reaching vision.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，忠恕移書史彌遠請取法孝宗，行三年喪，且曰：“孝宗始自踐祚，服勤子職凡二十有七年，今上自外邸入繼大統，未嚐躬一日定省之勞，欲報之德，視孝宗宜有加。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong ascended, Zhongshu sent a letter to Shi Miyuan begging to take Xiaozong as model and observe three years' mourning, saying, "Xiaozong from first treading the throne served diligently in the son's role for twenty-seven years; the present ruler from the outer residence entered to succeed the great succession, never personally performing one day's duty of morning and evening attendance—to repay that virtue, compared with Xiaozong there should be more."
translations.idiomatic: When Lizong ascended the throne, Zhongshu wrote to Shi Miyuan urging him to follow Xiaozong's example and observe three years' mourning. He said, "Xiaozong served his father dutifully for twenty-seven years after taking the throne. The present ruler succeeded from outside the palace and never once attended his father in person. To repay that debt of gratitude, he should mourn even more fully than Xiaozong."

sentences.zh: ”既而宰輔率百僚請太母同聽政，忠恕復貽書史彌遠，謂：“英宗以疾，仁、哲以幼，母後垂簾，有不容已，惟欽聖出於勉強，務從抑損。

translations.literal: " Soon the chief ministers led the hundred officials to beg the Grand Empress Dowager to hear government together; Zhongshu again sent a letter to Shi Miyuan, saying, "Yingzong because of illness, Ren and Zhe because of youth—the empress dowager curtained the court from necessity; only Qinsheng arose from compulsion and strove to restrain and reduce."
translations.idiomatic: " Soon the chief ministers led the officials to ask the Grand Empress Dowager to rule from behind the curtain. Zhongshu wrote again to Miyuan: "Yingzong was ill, Renzong and Zhezong were young—those cases required the empress dowager's regency. Only Qinsheng's regency was reluctant and deliberately restrained."

sentences.zh: 今吾君長矣，若姑援以請，此亦中策爾。

translations.literal: Now our ruler is grown; if for the moment you cite precedent in the request, this is also a middling stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Our ruler is grown now. If you cite precedent only provisionally in the request, that is at least a moderate course.

sentences.zh: ”詔群臣集議廟製，忠恕謂：“九廟非古。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered the hundred officials to assemble and discuss temple regulations; Zhongshu said, "Nine temples are not ancient."
translations.idiomatic: " When the court ordered officials to discuss temple regulations, Zhongshu said, "Nine ancestral temples are not an ancient institution."

sentences.zh: 若升先帝，則十世之廟昉於今日，於禮無稽。

translations.literal: If the former emperor is elevated, then the ten-generation temple begins today—in ritual there is no basis.
translations.idiomatic: If the former emperor is elevated, a ten-generation temple system would begin today, without any basis in ritual.

sentences.zh: 寶慶初，詔求直言，忠恕上封事，陳八事：

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoqing an edict sought frank speech; Zhongshu submitted a sealed memorial presenting eight matters:
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoqing the court called for frank speech. Zhongshu submitted a sealed memorial presenting eight points:

sentences.zh: 一曰天人之應，捷於影響。

translations.literal: First, the correspondence of heaven and man is swifter than shadow and echo.
translations.idiomatic: First, heaven and man respond to each other swifter than shadow follows form.

sentences.zh: 自冬徂春，雷雪非時，西霅、東淮，狂悖洊興。

translations.literal: From winter to spring thunder and snow came out of season; in western Zha and eastern Huai, violent rebellion arose repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: From winter to spring thunder and snow came out of season. In western Zha and eastern Huai, violent rebellions broke out repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 客星為妖，太白見晝，正統所係，不宜諉之分野。

translations.literal: Guest stars became omens; Venus appeared in daytime; the orthodox succession is involved—it is not fitting to shift blame to territorial divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Guest stars appeared as omens and Venus was seen by day. These concern the legitimacy of the dynasty and should not be blamed on territorial divisions.

sentences.zh: 二曰人道莫先乎孝，送死尤為大事。

translations.literal: Second, among human ways nothing comes before filial piety; sending off the dead is especially a great matter.
translations.idiomatic: Second, among human duties nothing comes before filial piety, and sending off the dead is especially important.

sentences.zh: 孝宗朝衣朝冠，皆以大布，迨寧考以適孫承重，光宗雖有疾，未嚐不服喪宮中也。

translations.literal: Xiaozong's court robes and court caps were all of coarse cloth; when Ningzong as eldest grandson bore the weight, though Guangzong had illness, he never failed to wear mourning in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong wore coarse cloth for court dress. When Ningzong as eldest grandson bore the mourning burden, Guangzong, though ill, never failed to wear mourning in the palace.

sentences.zh: 洎光宗上賓，權焰方張，莫有言者。

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended as guest on high, power's flame was just spreading—none spoke.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong died, powerful factions were ascendant and no one spoke out.

sentences.zh: 去秋禮寺受成胥吏，未嚐以義折衷。

translations.literal: Last autumn the Ministry of Rites clerks who received completion never once used righteousness to mediate.
translations.idiomatic: Last autumn the Ministry of Rites clerks who finalized the rites never judged them by moral principle.

sentences.zh: 慶元間，再期而祥，百僚始純服吉。

translations.literal: During Qingyuan, after two years came the auspicious rite and the hundred officials first wore pure auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingyuan, after two years came the auspicious rite, and only then did officials wear full auspicious dress.

sentences.zh: 今若甫經練祭，雖朝臣一帶之微，不復有凶吉之別，則是三年之喪降而為期，害理滋甚。

translations.literal: If now, having just passed the lian sacrifice, even the slight belt of court ministers no longer has mourning and auspicious distinction, then the three-year mourning is reduced to one year—harm to principle is ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: If now, right after the lian sacrifice, even the mourning belt of court ministers loses all distinction between mourning and auspicious dress, the three-year mourning is reduced to one year—a grave injury to ritual principle.

sentences.zh: 況人主執喪於內，而群工之服無異常日，是有父子而無君臣也。

translations.literal: Moreover the ruler observes mourning within while the host of officials' dress is no different from ordinary days—this is having father and son but not ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the ruler observes mourning within the palace while officials dress as on ordinary days—this preserves father and son but not ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 三曰太母方卻垂簾之請，而慶壽前期，陛下吉服稱觴，播為詩什，此世俗之見，非所以表儀於天下也。

translations.literal: Third, the Grand Empress Dowager has just declined the request to curtain the court, yet before the celebration of longevity Your Majesty in auspicious dress raised the cup and spread it as poetry—this is a vulgar view, not how to display model conduct to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the Grand Empress Dowager has just declined regency, yet before the longevity celebration Your Majesty raised a cup in auspicious dress and had the occasion turned into poetry. This is vulgar conduct, not how to set an example for the realm.

sentences.zh: 四曰陛下斬然在疚，大昏之期，固未暇問，然非豫講夙定，恐俚說乘間而入。

translations.literal: Fourth, Your Majesty is sharply in grief; the great wedding's time is naturally not yet attended to, yet if not prepared and settled long beforehand, I fear vulgar talk will seize the interval and enter.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, Your Majesty is deep in mourning. The wedding date is naturally not yet settled, but without long preparation, vulgar counsel may slip in at the first opportunity.

sentences.zh: 臣所望於今日者，亦曰嚴取舍而正法度，廣詢謀而協公議爾。

translations.literal: What your servant hopes for today is also to say: strictly choose and reject and correct law and institutions, broadly seek counsel and harmonize public discussion.
translations.idiomatic: What I hope for today is strict standards of selection, sound law and institutions, broad consultation, and harmony with public opinion.

sentences.zh: 五曰陛下於濟王之恩，自謂彌縫曲盡矣。

translations.literal: Fifth, Your Majesty's grace toward Prince Ji—you yourself say the patching and bending is thoroughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, Your Majesty believes you have done all you can for Prince Ji.

sentences.zh: 然不留京師，徙之外郡，不擇牧守，混之民居，一夫奮呼，闔城風靡，尋雖弭患，莫副初心。

translations.literal: Yet he was not kept in the capital but moved to outer prefectures; no choice of prefects and defenders; mixed with common residences—one man cried out and the whole city was swept; soon though the trouble was quelled, it did not match the original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was not kept in the capital but moved to outer prefectures, without careful choice of officials, lodged among commoners. One man's cry set the whole city in turmoil. Though the trouble was soon quelled, it fell far short of your original intent.

sentences.zh: 謂當此時，亟下哀詔，痛自引咎，優崇恤典，選立嗣子，則陛下所以身處者，庶幾無憾，而造訛騰謗者，靡所致力。

translations.literal: I say at this time urgently issue a mournful edict, painfully blame yourself, generously honor condolence rites, select and establish an heir—then Your Majesty's position could nearly be without regret, and those who manufacture slander would have nowhere to exert effort.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment you should have issued a mournful edict, accepted blame, honored him with full rites, and chosen an heir. Then your position would have been nearly without reproach, and slanderers would have had no foothold.

sentences.zh: 自始至今，率誤於含糊，而猶不此之思，臣所不解也。

translations.literal: From beginning to now you have consistently erred through vagueness, yet still do not think on this—what your servant cannot understand.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning you have consistently erred through vagueness, yet still do not reconsider—I cannot understand it.

sentences.zh: 六曰近世憸佞之徒，凡直言正論，率指為好名歸過；

translations.literal: Sixth, in recent times flatterers and sycophants—whatever frank and upright discourse invariably label as loving fame and shifting blame;
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, in recent times flatterers label every frank and upright statement as mere love of fame or shifting blame;

sentences.zh: 夫好名歸過，其自為者非也，若首萌逆億厭惡之心，則自今言者望風見疑，此危國之鴆毒。

translations.literal: Loving fame and shifting blame—those who do it themselves are wrong; if first sprouting a contrary heart of suspicion and disgust, then from now speakers will see wind and be doubted—this is the poison that endangers the state.
translations.idiomatic: Loving fame and shifting blame are wrong in themselves, but if you first harbor suspicion and disgust toward speakers, then from now on remonstrators will be doubted on sight—this is poison to the state.

sentences.zh: 七曰當今名流雖已褒顯，而搜羅未廣，遺才尚多。

translations.literal: Seventh, though famous currents today have been praised and displayed, the search has not been broad and overlooked talent is still many.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, though some eminent men have been honored, the search has not been broad and many talents remain overlooked.

sentences.zh: 經明行修如柴中行、陳孔碩、楊簡，識高氣直如陳宓、徐僑、傅伯成，僉論所推：史筆如李心傅，何惜一官，不俾與聞。

translations.literal: Classics clear and conduct cultivated like Chai Zhongxing, Chen Kongshuo, Yang Jian; insight high and spirit straight like Chen Mi, Xu Qiao, Fu Bocheng—unanimous opinion promotes them; historical brush like Li Xinfu—why spare one office and not let him participate in deliberation?
translations.idiomatic: Men of learning and integrity such as Chai Zhongxing, Chen Kongshuo, and Yang Jian; men of high insight and upright spirit such as Chen Mi, Xu Qiao, and Fu Bocheng—all widely praised. A historian such as Li Xinfu—why withhold an office and deny him a voice?

sentences.zh: 況邇來取人，以名節為矯激，以忠讜為迂疏，以介潔為不通，以寬厚為無用，以趣辦為強敏，以拱默為靖共，以迎合為適時，以操切為任事。

translations.literal: Moreover in recent selection of men: taking name and integrity as pretentious excess, loyal frankness as pedantic remoteness, integrity and cleanliness as lack of accommodation, generosity as uselessness, rapid fulfillment as strong keenness, folded silence as tranquil accord, currying favor as timely fit, harsh urgency as bearing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in recent appointments: integrity is called pretentiousness, frank loyalty pedantry, scrupulousness inflexibility, generosity uselessness, rapid fulfillment keenness, silence dutifulness, flattery timeliness, and harshness efficiency.

sentences.zh: 是以正士不遇，小人見親。

translations.literal: Therefore upright gentlemen are not met while petty men are seen and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Thus upright gentlemen go unused while petty men are favored.

sentences.zh: 八曰士習日異，民生益艱。

translations.literal: Eighth, scholarly custom daily differs and people's livelihood grows ever harder.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, scholarly customs grow daily more corrupt and the people's livelihood grows ever harder.

sentences.zh: 第宅之麗，聲伎之美，服用之侈，饋遺之珍，向來宗戚、閹官猶或間見，今縉紳士大夫殆過之。

translations.literal: Splendor of mansions, beauty of music and performers, extravagance of dress and use, rarity of gifts—formerly imperial kin and eunuch officials still appeared occasionally; now gentry and scholar-officials nearly surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid mansions, fine entertainers, extravagant dress, costly gifts—once seen only among imperial kin and eunuchs, now gentry and scholar-officials nearly surpass them.

sentences.zh: 公家之財，視為己物。

translations.literal: Public wealth is regarded as one's own possessions.
translations.idiomatic: Public funds are treated as private property.

sentences.zh: 薦舉、獄訟，軍伎、吏役、僧道、富民，凡可以得賄者，無不為也。

translations.literal: Recommendations, lawsuits, military performers, clerks and runners, monks and Daoists, wealthy commoners—whatever could obtain bribes, none was not done.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendations, lawsuits, military entertainers, clerks, monks, Daoists, wealthy commoners—whatever could yield a bribe was exploited.

sentences.zh: 至其避譏媒進，往往分獻厥餘。

translations.literal: As for avoiding ridicule and mediating advancement, they often divide and offer the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid criticism and advance their favorites, they often share the spoils among themselves.

sentences.zh: 欲基本之不搖，殆卻行而求前也。

translations.literal: Wishing the foundation not to shake is nearly walking backward to seek forward progress.
translations.idiomatic: To wish the foundation unshaken while acting thus is like walking backward and expecting to advance.

sentences.zh: 疏入，朝紳傳誦。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, court gentry passed it around reciting.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, court officials passed it around and recited it.

sentences.zh: 始魏了翁嚐勉忠恕以“植立名節，無隤家聲”。

translations.literal: Earlier Wei Liaoweng had urged Zhongshu to "establish name and integrity, do not tumble the family's reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liaoweng had once urged Zhongshu to "establish your integrity and do not dishonor the family name."

sentences.zh: 及是歎曰：“忠獻有後矣！

translations.literal: On this he sighed and said, "Zhongxian has posterity!"
translations.idiomatic: On reading it he sighed, "Zhongxian has a worthy descendant!"

sentences.zh: ”真德秀聞之，更納交焉。

translations.literal: " Zhen Dexiu heard of it and further sought his friendship.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen Dexiu heard of it and sought his friendship.

sentences.zh: 忠恕又因輪對，引以伯父栻告孝宗之語曰：“當求曉事之臣，不求辦事之臣；

translations.literal: Zhongshu again on rotating audience cited his uncle Shi's words to Xiaozong: "One should seek ministers who understand affairs, not ministers who merely handle affairs;"
translations.idiomatic: At rotating audience Zhongshu cited his uncle Zhang Shi's advice to Xiaozong: "Seek ministers who understand affairs, not ministers who merely get things done;"

sentences.zh: 欲求伏節死義之臣，必求犯顏敢諫之臣。

translations.literal: if one wishes ministers who bow to integrity and die for righteousness, one must seek ministers who offend the countenance and dare remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: if you wish ministers who uphold integrity and die for principle, you must seek ministers who dare remonstrate to your face.

sentences.zh: ”語益剴切。

translations.literal: " His words grew ever more earnest and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: " His words grew ever more earnest and forceful.

sentences.zh: 忠恕自知不為時所容，力請外補，遂以直秘閣知贛州。

translations.literal: Zhongshu knew himself not tolerated by the times, forcefully begged outer appointment, and was then made Direct Attendant of the Secret Repository and magistrate of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he was not tolerated at court, Zhongshu pressed for an outside appointment and was made Direct Attendant of the Secret Repository and prefect of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 抵郡才兩月，言者指為朋比，落職，降兩官，罷。

translations.literal: Reaching the prefecture after only two months, critics pointed to factional collusion; he was dismissed from office, demoted two ranks, and removed.
translations.idiomatic: After only two months in office, critics accused him of factional collusion. He was dismissed, demoted two ranks, and removed.

sentences.zh: 紹定三年，復元官，進秩一等，提舉衝佑觀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoding his original office was restored, rank advanced one grade, and he was made Superintendent of the Chongyou Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: In 1230 his original rank was restored with one additional grade, and he was made Superintendent of the Chongyou Abbey.

sentences.zh: 卒，遷一官致仕。

translations.literal: He died; advanced one rank and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He died after receiving one final promotion and retirement.

sentences.zh: 魏了翁嚐許忠恕“拳拳體國似浚，撥繁剸劇似其父枃，斂華就實則有誌義理之學，嚐有聞乎栻之教矣”。

translations.literal: Wei Liaoweng once praised Zhongshu: "Earnestly embodying the state like Jun, sorting complexity and cutting urgency like his father Biao, gathering splendor toward substance then having the learning that aspires to principle and righteousness—he has heard Shi's teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liaoweng once praised Zhongshu: "He serves the state with the same earnest devotion as Jun, handles complex affairs with his father Biao's skill, and pursues substance over show with the learning of principle and righteousness he learned from Zhang Shi's teaching."

sentences.zh: 唐璘，字伯玉，古田人。

translations.literal: Tang Lin, courtesy name Boyu, was a man of Gutian.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Lin, styled Boyu, was from Gutian.

sentences.zh: 遊太學。

translations.literal: He studied at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十年舉進士，時台臣李安行奏次對官不許論邊事，璘對策極詆之，曰：“吾始進，可壞於天子之庭乎？

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination; at the time Censor Li Anxing memorialized that rotating audience officials might not discuss border affairs; Lin in his policy response fiercely denounced this, saying, "I am just entering—can I be ruined in the Son of Heaven's court?"
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1217. When Censor Li Anxing memorialized that rotating audience officials must not discuss border affairs, Lin's policy response fiercely denounced this: "I am just entering service—shall I be silenced in the Son of Heaven's court?"

sentences.zh: ”調吳縣尉，有殺人於貨挾其舟亡者，有司求賊急，屠者自告吾兒實殺之，兒亦自誣伏。

translations.literal: " He was transferred as Wu County sheriff; there was one who killed for goods and fled with his boat; officials urgently sought the culprit; a butcher confessed himself saying my son really killed him, and the son also falsely confessed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed sheriff of Wu County. A man had killed for goods and fled by boat. Officials urgently sought the culprit. A butcher confessed that his son had done it, and the son also falsely confessed.

sentences.zh: 璘問：“舟安在？

translations.literal: Lin asked, "Where is the boat?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin asked, "Where is the boat?"

sentences.zh: 錢何用？

translations.literal: What was the money used for?"
translations.idiomatic: What was done with the money?"

sentences.zh: ”其辭差，為緩之，果得賊太湖，與舟俱至，舉縣感服。

translations.literal: " Their words differed; he slowed the case; indeed he obtained the culprit at Tai Lake with the boat together arriving—the whole county was moved to submission.
translations.idiomatic: " Their accounts did not match. He slowed the case, found the real culprit at Tai Lake with the boat, and won the admiration of the whole county.

sentences.zh: 縣有勢家治圃，將鑿渠通舟，繆言古有渠，常平使者主之。

translations.literal: The county had a powerful family tending a garden who wished to dig a canal for boats, falsely saying there was an ancient canal; the Ever-Normal envoy presided over it.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful family in the county tending a garden planned to dig a canal for boats, falsely claiming an ancient canal had existed there. The Ever-Normal envoy supported the project.

sentences.zh: 璘視乾道故籍，則誠民田也，力爭，迕使者意，移監縣稅。

translations.literal: Lin looked at the Qiandao-era old registers—it was truly common people's fields; he argued forcefully, going against the envoy's intent, and was transferred to supervise county taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Lin checked the Qiandao-era land registers and found it was truly commoners' farmland. He argued forcefully against the project, offended the envoy, and was transferred to supervise county taxes.

sentences.zh: 璘遂以直聞。

translations.literal: Lin then became known for uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Lin thereby became known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 調瑞州學教授，用白鹿洞教法，崇禮讓，後文藝，士翕然知向。

translations.literal: Transferred as professor of Ruizhou school, he used the Bailudong teaching method, honored ritual and yielding, placed literary arts after, and scholars uniformly knew where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: He was made professor at Ruizhou school, using the Bailudong teaching method. He honored ritual and deference, placed literary arts second, and scholars turned to him uniformly.

sentences.zh: 監行在榷貨務門。

translations.literal: He supervised the gate of the capital monopoly goods office.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the capital monopoly goods office.

sentences.zh: 辟淮東運司催轄綱運官。

translations.literal: Recruited as Huai-East transport commission officer urging and overseeing transport-cord officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as transport officer for Huai-East, overseeing grain transport.

sentences.zh: 屬出師楚州，盡瘁焉。

translations.literal: When troops were sent out from Chuzhou he exhausted himself therein.
translations.idiomatic: When troops marched out from Chuzhou he exhausted himself in the effort.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，以金人據淮陰，欲乘勢取之。

translations.literal: Victory was reported; because Jin people held Huaiyin, they wished to take advantage of momentum to seize it.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, the court learned the Jin held Huaiyin and wished to seize it while momentum favored them.

sentences.zh: 璘言：“捷奏多誇，詎得信乎？

translations.literal: Lin said, "Victory reports are mostly exaggerated—how can they be believed?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "Victory reports are mostly exaggerated—how can they be believed?"

sentences.zh: 須聚兵二十萬，日費米斛餘五千，緡錢餘二萬，調夫幾萬人，僅能使賊全師北去。

translations.literal: One must gather two hundred thousand troops, daily spend more than five thousand hu of rice, more than twenty thousand strings of cash, conscript tens of thousands of laborers—only then could the enemy's whole army be made to go north.
translations.idiomatic: It would require two hundred thousand troops, more than five thousand hu of rice per day, more than twenty thousand strings of cash, and tens of thousands of laborers—merely to drive the enemy's whole army north.

sentences.zh: 今出沒漣、海，謀結北邊，政欲迭出撓我，憂方大爾。

translations.literal: Now they appear and vanish between Lian and Hai, plotting to connect with the northern frontier, just wishing to come out repeatedly and harass us—the worry is still great.
translations.idiomatic: Now they raid between Lian and Hai, plotting with the northern frontier, intending to harass us repeatedly—the danger is still grave.

sentences.zh: 淮陰緊壘與楚城等，濠之廣又過之，我士疲丁困，可一拔得乎？

translations.literal: Huaiyin's tight fortifications equal Chucheng; the moat's breadth surpasses it; our soldiers are weary and laborers exhausted—can it be seized in one pull?
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyin's fortifications match Chucheng's, and its moat is even wider. Our troops are weary and laborers exhausted—can it be taken at one stroke?

sentences.zh: 恢復，美名也，而賈實禍，仆竊危之。

translations.literal: Recovery is a fine name, but it purchases real calamity—I privately fear it.
translations.idiomatic: Recovery is a fine name, but it buys real disaster—I fear it deeply.

sentences.zh: ”不聽，製司恥楚城之捷自趙範與葵出，議贖淮陰二城為功。

translations.literal: " He was not heeded; the pacification office was shamed that Chucheng's victory came from Zhao Fan and Kui, and discussed ransoming the two Huaiyin cities as merit.
translations.idiomatic: " He was not heeded. The pacification office, shamed that Chucheng's victory came from Zhao Fan and Kui, proposed ransoming the two Huaiyin cities as a triumph.

sentences.zh: 洎聞金變，即轉攻之，我師死傷者六萬，璘在兵間憤之，著《讜論》，直書其事上之。

translations.literal: When they heard the Jin situation changed they immediately turned to attack; our army dead and wounded numbered sixty thousand; Lin among the troops was angry, composed Straight Talk, and directly wrote the matter and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard the Jin situation had changed, they immediately attacked. Our army suffered sixty thousand dead and wounded. Lin, amid the troops, wrote Straight Talk and submitted a frank account of what had happened.

sentences.zh: 知晉陵縣，鄰州田訟，至有泣訴諸使願送晉陵可否者。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Jinling County—neighboring prefectures' land lawsuits, to the point that some wept appealing to commissioners wishing to send cases to Jinling for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Jinling County, litigants from neighboring prefectures wept before commissioners begging to have their land disputes sent to Jinling for judgment.

sentences.zh: 製置使陳韡留守建康，辟為通判，舉府事以聽。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Chen Kan remained to guard Jiankang, recruited him as vice prefect, and entrusted all prefectural affairs to his hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Chen Kan, guarding Jiankang, recruited him as vice prefect and entrusted all prefectural affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 監六部門，擢監察御史，台吏且至，璘皇駭趨避不敢詣闕。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Six Department Gates; elevated to Surveillance Censor; censorate clerks were about to arrive—Lin in panic rushed to avoid and dared not approach the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the Six Department Gates and was elevated to Surveillance Censor. When censorate clerks were about to arrive, Lin fled in panic and dared not approach the palace.

sentences.zh: 母曰：“人言此官好，汝何得憂乎？

translations.literal: His mother said, "People say this office is good—why should you worry?"
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "People say this is a fine post—why are you worried?"

sentences.zh: ”璘曰：“此官須為朝廷爭是非，一咈上意或迕權貴，恐重為大人累，何得不憂？

translations.literal: " Lin said, "This office must dispute right and wrong for the court; one offense against the ruler's intent or clash with the powerful—I fear greatly burdening you, my lady—how can I not worry?"
translations.idiomatic: " Lin said, "This office must speak truth to power for the court. One word against the emperor's will or the mighty could burden you deeply—how could I not worry?"

sentences.zh: ”母曰：“而第盡言，吾有而兄在，忽憂。

translations.literal: " His mother said, "You just speak fully—I have your elder brother here; do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: " His mother said, "Speak your mind fully. Your elder brother is here—do not worry."

sentences.zh: ”璘拜謝，入就職。

translations.literal: " Lin bowed in thanks and entered to take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: " Lin bowed in thanks and took up his post.

sentences.zh: 故事，御史惟常服拜下，有論奏繳進，至是獨召對緝熙殿，令服窄衫麵讀。

translations.literal: By precedent censors only bowed in ordinary dress; memorials on policy were submitted in writing; on this occasion he alone was summoned to audience at the Jixi Hall and ordered to wear a narrow-sleeved shirt and read face to face.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent censors bowed in ordinary dress and submitted written memorials. This time he alone was summoned to the Jixi Hall and ordered to wear a narrow-sleeved shirt and read his memorial in person.

sentences.zh: 首疏奏：“天變而至於怒，民怨而幾於離，海宇將傾，天下有不可勝諱之慮。

translations.literal: His first memorial said, "Heavenly changes have reached anger; people's resentment nearly reaches separation; the seas and lands will topple; the realm has worries that cannot all be tabooed."
translations.idiomatic: His first memorial said, "Heaven's wrath has broken forth, the people's resentment nears revolt, the realm totters, and the court faces fears it dare not speak aloud."

sentences.zh: 陛下謂此何時，縱欲累德，文過飾非，疏遠正人，狎昵戚宦，濁亂朝政，自取覆亡。

translations.literal: Your Majesty—what time is this? Yet you wish to heap up virtue, gloss faults and adorn errors, keep distant upright men, be intimate with kin and eunuchs, muddy and disorder court governance, and bring ruin on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, what time is this? Yet you seek to pile up merit, gloss over faults, keep upright men at a distance, dally with kin and eunuchs, corrupt court governance, and court your own ruin.

sentences.zh: 宰相用時文之才為經世之具，不顧民命，輕挑兵端，不度事宜，頓空國帑。

translations.literal: The chief minister uses the talent of fashionable prose as the tool to order the age, heedless of people's lives, lightly provokes military conflict, does not measure affairs' suitability, and suddenly empties the state treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister treats fashionable literary talent as statecraft, heedless of the people's lives, lightly provokes war, misjudges affairs, and has emptied the treasury.

sentences.zh: 委政厥子，內交商人，賄塗大開，小雅盡廢。

translations.literal: He entrusts government to his son, connects inside with merchants, the path of bribes is widely opened, and the Minor Odes are wholly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusts power to his son, colludes with merchants, opens wide the path of bribery, and has abandoned the Minor Odes of governance.

sentences.zh: 瑣瑣姻婭，敢預邪謀，視國事如俳優，以神器為奇貨，都人側目，朝士痛心。

translations.literal: Petty affinal kin dare participate in wicked plots, regard state affairs as acrobats, take the sacred vessel as rare goods—the capital's people look askance, court gentlemen ache in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Petty in-laws dare join wicked plots, treat state affairs as a play, and the imperial regalia as merchandise for profit. The capital looks on in dismay; court officials ache with grief.

sentences.zh: 盍正無將之誅，以著不忠之戒。

translations.literal: Why not correct the punishment for those with no commander, to display the warning against disloyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Why not impose the punishment for disloyal subjects, to make an example of treachery?

sentences.zh: 崔與之操行類楊綰，雖修途莫景，力不逮心，而命下之日，聞者興起。

translations.literal: Cui Yuzhi's conduct resembled Yang Guan; though on the cultivated path there was no resting in shade and strength did not reach the heart, yet on the day the appointment came down those who heard were uplifted.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuzhi's conduct resembled Yang Guan's. Though his strength did not match his ideals, the day his appointment was announced uplifted all who heard it.

sentences.zh: 喬行簡頗識大體，朝望稍孚，而除授偏私，事多遺忘。

translations.literal: Qiao Xingjian fairly understood the larger pattern; court expectation was somewhat fulfilled; yet appointments were partial and private, and many matters were forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xingjian understood the larger pattern and enjoyed some court esteem, but his appointments were partial and he forgot many matters.

sentences.zh: 宜擇家相，讚宗子，輔民物，以慰父母之望，毋使天變浸極，人心愈離也。

translations.literal: It is fitting to choose a family chief minister, assist the imperial scion, support the people and things, to comfort the parents' hope—do not let heavenly changes gradually reach the extreme and people's hearts grow ever more estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Choose a chief minister of proven family, support the imperial heir, aid the people, and comfort your forebears' hopes—do not let heaven's warnings grow extreme and the people's hearts drift further away.

sentences.zh: ”上為改容。

translations.literal: " The emperor's expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's expression changed.

sentences.zh: 又請號召土豪，經理荊、襄，亟擇帥臣，安集淮西，帝嘉納；

translations.literal: He also begged to summon local strongmen, manage Jing and Xiang, urgently choose commanders, and settle Western Huai—the emperor praised and accepted;
translations.idiomatic: He also urged summoning local strongmen, organizing Jing and Xiang, urgently choosing commanders, and stabilizing Western Huai. The emperor commended and accepted this advice;

sentences.zh: 至問邊事甚悉。

translations.literal: and questioned border affairs very thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: and questioned him thoroughly on border affairs.

sentences.zh: 璘感激知遇，自是彈擊無所避，再疏：“鄭清之妄庸誤國，乞褫職罷祠。

translations.literal: Lin, moved by this recognition, from then on impeached without avoidance; a second memorial: "Zheng Qingzhi is reckless, mediocre, and misleads the state—I beg to strip his office and abolish his temple post."
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for this recognition, Lin from then on impeached without restraint. A second memorial said, "Zheng Qingzhi is mediocre and misleads the state. Strip his office and abolish his temple appointment."

sentences.zh: 其子士昌，招權納賄，拔庸將為統帥，起贓吏為守臣，乞削籍廢棄。

translations.literal: His son Shichang gathers power and accepts bribes, elevates mediocre generals as commanders, raises corrupt officials as defending ministers—I beg to strike them from the registers and cast them out.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shichang abuses power and takes bribes, elevates mediocre generals to command, and restores corrupt officials as prefects. I beg that they be struck from the registers and cast out.

sentences.zh: 鄭性之懦而多私，黨庇奸庸，臣受其改官舉狀，嚐蒙薦之陛下，國事至此，不敢顧私。

translations.literal: Zheng Xingzhi is timid and much given to private interest, factions sheltering villains and mediocrities; your servant received his recommendation for office change and once was honored to recommend him to Your Majesty—state affairs have reached this point; I dare not consider private interest.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xingzhi is timid and self-serving, sheltering villains and mediocrities in faction. I once received his recommendation and even commended him to Your Majesty, but with state affairs at this pass I dare not consider private ties.

sentences.zh: 李鳴復甘心諂鄭損，得薦入朝，適清之議張天綱之獄，迎合從輕，遂擢台端。

translations.literal: Li Mingfu willingly flattered Zheng Sun, obtained recommendation to enter court; it happened that Qingzhi discussed Zhang Tiangang's case, curried favor to lighten it, and was then elevated to the censorate summit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mingfu willingly flattered Zheng Sun and won recommendation to court. When Qingzhi handled Zhang Tiangang's case, Mingfu curried favor to lighten the sentence and was elevated to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 會趙桄夫遣史寅午囑清之父子，鳴復又結寅午得登政府。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhao Kuangfu sent Shi Yinwu to instruct Qingzhi father and son; Mingfu again connected with Yinwu and obtained entry to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangfu sent Shi Yinwu to instruct the Qingzhi family, and Mingfu allied with Yinwu to enter the government.

sentences.zh: ”會杜範亦論鳴復，不行，而範去，璘遂力丐外，疏七上，授廣西運判，改知嘉興府，尋改江東運判。

translations.literal: " It happened that Du Fan also impeached Mingfu—nothing was done; Fan departed; Lin then forcefully begged for outer appointment, seven memorials submitted, appointed Guangxi transport vice commissioner, changed to magistrate of Jiaxing Prefecture, soon changed to Jiangdong transport vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: " Du Fan also impeached Mingfu, but nothing was done. When Fan left office, Lin pressed hard for an outside post, submitting seven memorials. He was made Guangxi transport vice commissioner, then prefect of Jiaxing, and soon Jiangdong transport vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時邊事急，置四察訪使，就詔璘分建康、太平、池州、江西。

translations.literal: Border affairs were urgent; four inspection envoys were established; an edict ordered Lin to divide Jiankang, Taiping, Chizhou, and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: With border affairs urgent, four inspection envoys were appointed, and Lin was ordered by edict to oversee Jiankang, Taiping, Chizhou, and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 璘揭榜馬前，谘所部以利害，又戒土豪團結漁業水手、茶鹽舟夫、蘆丁，悉備燎舟之具，人人思奮。

translations.literal: Lin posted a proclamation before his horse, consulted his jurisdiction on advantage and harm, and also warned local strongmen to unite fishing sailors, tea-and-salt boatmen, and reed cutters, fully prepare fire-ship equipment—every man thought to exert himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lin posted a proclamation before his horse and consulted his jurisdiction on strategy. He urged local strongmen to organize fishing sailors, tea-and-salt boatmen, and reed cutters, fully equip fire ships, and rouse every man to fight.

sentences.zh: 即選將總二州兵舟以耀敵，檄當塗宿設戰具，防采石，撥和糴續生券，且奏損總領所錢二十萬緡助江防，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Immediately he chose generals to command the two prefectures' troops and boats to display before the enemy; dispatched orders to Dangtu to set battle equipment overnight, defend Caishi, allocate harmonized purchase and renewal life certificates, and memorialized to reduce two hundred thousand strings from the superintendency to aid river defense—the army's reputation greatly rose.
translations.idiomatic: He chose generals to command troops and boats from two prefectures to display strength before the enemy, ordered Dangtu to prepare battle equipment overnight, defended Caishi, allocated grain purchases and relief certificates, and memorialized to divert two hundred thousand strings from the superintendency to aid river defense. Military morale soared.

sentences.zh: 尋升直華文閣、知廣州、廣東經略安撫使。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Huawen Pavilion, magistrate of Guangzhou, and Guangdong Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Direct Attendant of the Huawen Pavilion, prefect of Guangzhou, and Guangdong Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 梅州寇作，璘示以威信，寇尋息。

translations.literal: Bandits arose in Meizhou; Lin displayed authority and trust; the bandits soon ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Meizhou, Lin displayed authority and good faith, and the unrest soon subsided.

sentences.zh: 江淮旱，議下廣右和糴，璘言：“公家赤立，糴本無所辦，終恐日取於民，非臣不敢撥本，召釁重朝廷多事之憂。

translations.literal: Jiang-Huai drought—the court discussed sending harmonized purchase to the far south; Lin said, "The public coffers stand bare; purchase capital has nowhere to be raised; in the end I fear daily taking from the people—it is not that your servant dares not allocate capital, but to summon trouble and add to the court's worry in many affairs."
translations.idiomatic: During drought in Jiang-Huai the court discussed grain purchases from the far south. Lin said, "The treasury is empty and there is no capital for purchases. In the end the cost will be taken from the people daily. It is not that I refuse to allocate funds, but to provoke trouble when the court already faces so many crises."

sentences.zh: ”明年上章乞致仕，帝思見之，亟命入奏，擢太常少卿。

translations.literal: " The next year he submitted a memorial begging retirement; the emperor wished to see him and urgently ordered him to enter and report; he was elevated to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: " The next year he memorialized to retire. The emperor wished to see him, urgently summoned him to court, and made him Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 尋丁內艱，璘居喪哀毀不食，久之疾革，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he mourned an inner bereavement; Lin in mourning was grief-stricken, wasted, and did not eat; after long illness became critical and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he mourned a close relative. Lin grieved so deeply he would not eat. After a long illness he died.

sentences.zh: 璘立台僅百日，世謂再見唐介，至切劘上躬，盡言無隱，帝益嚴憚之。

translations.literal: Lin stood at the censorate only a hundred days; the age said Tang Jie was seen again; he was utmost in cutting and sharpening toward the ruler's person, speaking fully without concealment—the emperor grew ever more strictly in awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: Lin served at the censorate only a hundred days, and the age said Tang Jie had appeared again. He spoke bluntly to the emperor without concealment, and the emperor grew ever more wary of him.

sentences.zh: 居官大節，則母教之助為多。

translations.literal: In holding office with great integrity, his mother's teaching aided him much.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity in office owed much to his mother's teaching.

sentences.zh: 論曰：觀高定子在西陲，政業著聞矣。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Observing Gao Dingzi on the western frontier, his governmental achievements were renowned.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Gao Dingzi's achievements on the western frontier were renowned.

sentences.zh: 斯得屢起而屢仆於權臣之手，及其再起，宋事已非。

translations.literal: Side repeatedly rose and repeatedly fell at the hands of powerful ministers; when he rose again, Song affairs were already not as they had been.
translations.idiomatic: Side rose repeatedly only to fall at the hands of powerful ministers, and when he rose again the Song cause was already lost.

sentences.zh: 張忠恕論濟邸事，有父祖風焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongshu on the matter of Prince Ji's residence had the wind of father and grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongshu in speaking on Prince Ji's affair showed the spirit of his father and grandfather.

sentences.zh: 唐璘者，亦可謂古之遺直。

translations.literal: Tang Lin may also be called a surviving upright man of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Lin may also be called a surviving upright man of the ancients.
